## `0051` — First projection-layer landing (`HypothesisProjection`); single-hypothesis read-side materialization over the §2.5 lifecycle event chain; Charter §2.5 BC3 deferred-state read shape now operationally observable

- **Status:** accepted.
- **Date:** 2026-05-20.

- **Context:** [`§0050`](#0050--sixth-final-category-iii-lifecycle-event-behavioralclustersplit-lands-structural-inverse-of-merge-6-of-6-lifecycle-operations-now-structurally-observable-25-lifecycle-surface-complete) completed the §2.5 lifecycle surface — six concrete lifecycle event types (formation, promotion, demotion, dissolution, merge, split) are now writable. Every entry in the §0045–§0050 arc carried a Consequences carry-forward naming **"Projection over the full lifecycle event chain"** as deferred per Charter §2.5 BC3 (which forbids storing "current state" as a substrate row — the substrate stores immutable lifecycle events; current state must be reconstructed by replaying them). With the substrate-write side complete, projection is no longer blocked on missing input. This entry lands the first projection-layer surface: single-hypothesis on-demand read-side materialization.

  The projection layer surfaced three structural choices decided in this entry against current ground:

  - **On-demand vs materialized.** Option (A): on-demand walk via `substrate.WalkEvents` per call. Option (B): materialized projection table maintained as a side-effect of substrate writes. Option (A) chosen at this layer per inception-phase substrate sizes (linear walk is acceptable cost) AND the constitutional-minimalism principle (CLAUDE.md §7 — ceremony without behavioral consequence is rejected): a materialized projection table is additional state to invalidate, backup, and verify; the read-side cost of the linear walk does not yet justify that complexity. A follow-on landing may introduce projection-side indexing if the linear walk becomes a bottleneck — that landing will arrive against the new operational ground rather than be predicted now.

  - **Layering: read-only vs read-write coupling.** Option (A): `internal/projection` depends only on `substrate` (for the walk) + `genproto/events/v1` (for unmarshaling lifecycle payloads). Option (B): `internal/projection` reuses lifecycle event constants + helpers from `internal/hypothesis`. Option (A) chosen: projection is read-only; coupling it to the writer surface (`hypothesis` package) would invite circular dependencies as projection-driven inference work lands. The five lifecycle-event message-type discriminator constants are duplicated in `projection.go` rather than imported from `hypothesis.go`; the duplication is structural (3 lines × 5 constants) and acceptable per constitutional-minimalism — drift is detected at compile time the first time either side updates a constant without the other.

  - **State precedence rules.** The projection MUST collapse the per-formation lifecycle history into a single `State` enum value for operator-facing reporting. Precedence chosen (highest → lowest): Dissolved beats everything (terminal per §0048); SplitInto beats MergedInto when both apply (split is the terminal partition); MergedInto beats the promote/demote arc; within promote/demote, Demoted when a demotion targets the latest promotion, otherwise Promoted; default Forming. The precedence is an operational convention of the projection, NOT a Charter invariant — a future revision may redact it. The chosen ordering matches the read shape operators are most likely to want (terminal states surface; in-flight states are visible via the full `LifecycleHistory` regardless of the collapsed `State`).

- **Decision:** Land `HypothesisProjection` as the first projection-layer surface, with four structural moves:

  1. **`internal/projection` package** at [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/projection.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/projection.go). New package; not yet a stable read-side API — the inception-phase posture per [`§0027`](#0027--substrate-technology-protocol-buffer-canonical-substrate-on-sqlite-blob-store-third-technology-rfc-per-0022-pivot) applies. Types:

     - `State` (string enum): `forming`, `promoted`, `demoted`, `dissolved`, `merged_into`, `split_into`.
     - `LifecycleEntry`: typed record of one lifecycle event reaching the projected formation (Type = Protobuf descriptor full name, EventHash, EventTime).
     - `HypothesisProjection`: materialized view containing `FormationHash`, computed `State`, and per-lifecycle-type pointers (`LatestPromotion`, `LatestDemotion`, `Dissolution`, `MergedInto`, `SplitInto`) for operator inspection + full chronological `LifecycleHistory`.

     Message-type discriminators duplicated as package-level constants per the layering choice above.

  2. **`ProjectHypothesis(ctx, sub, formationHash)` entry point** at the same file. Two-pass walk:
     - Pass one: collect every promotion event targeting the formation (needed to resolve demotions — demotion targets a promotion hash, not the formation directly).
     - Pass two: collect demotions targeting any promotion of this formation; dissolutions targeting the formation; merges containing the formation in their antecedent set; splits whose antecedent IS the formation.
     - Sort `LifecycleHistory` ascending by `EventTime`; compute terminal `State` per the precedence rules above.

     Errors:
     - `ErrFormationNotFound`: target hash does not resolve to any substrate row.
     - `ErrTargetNotFormation`: target hash resolves to a row whose `message_type` is not `BehavioralClusterFormation` (parallel to `hypothesis.ErrTargetWrongType` but read-side; the projection layer surfaces its own sentinels to maintain layering).

  3. **`cmd/hypothesis-state` operator interface** at [`services/ingestion/cmd/hypothesis-state/main.go`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/hypothesis-state/main.go). Tenth operational binary alongside `verify`, `orphan-cleanup`, `derive-operational-session`, `form-hypothesis`, `promote-hypothesis`, `demote-hypothesis`, `dissolve-hypothesis`, `merge-hypotheses`, `split-hypothesis`. First binary in the **read-only** classification — every prior binary either commits substrate rows (`form-hypothesis`, the five lifecycle operators), audits the substrate's hash-chain consistency or maintains the blob-store (`verify`, `orphan-cleanup`), or derives Category II (`derive-operational-session`). Options: `-formation-event-hash` (required, 64-char hex). Structured JSON output describing the full projection. Exit codes: **0** success; **2** tool/configuration error; **3** formation-not-found or target-not-formation.

  4. **Test coverage** at [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/projection_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/projection_test.go). 11 tests covering each terminal state (forming, promoted, demoted, dissolved, merged-into, split-into) plus precedence edges (dissolution-beats-promotion, split-beats-merge-against-different-formation), re-promotion arc returning to promoted, lifecycle-history chronological ordering, unknown-formation rejection, wrong-type-target rejection.

- **Constitutional review:** No Charter invariant amended. No frozen-section prose modified. Respects [§2.1](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#21-observational-integrity) — the projection layer is strictly read-only over the immutable substrate; no lifecycle event is created, modified, or interpreted in a way that would constitute a §2.1 violation. Respects [§2.2](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#22-epistemic-separation) — the projection's `State` field is an operational summary of the lifecycle chain, NOT a category claim about the underlying phenomenon (the phenomenon claim lives in the formation event itself; the projection reports lifecycle position). Respects [§2.3](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#23-provenance-integrity) — every projection entry references its producing lifecycle event by content-hash; the projection is reconstructible from the same substrate state regardless of when or where it is computed. Respects [§2.5](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness) — projects exactly the six lifecycle operations defined at the abstract `Hypothesis` type level. Respects [§2.5 BC3](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness) — explicitly implements the BC3-mandated read shape ("the hypothesis's current state is a projection over the operation event history") as a discrete operationally-observable surface, completing the structural circuit that §2.5 BC3 specifies. Respects [`§0045`](#0045--first-category-iii-hypothesis-subtype-behavioralcluster-formation-lands-25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness-structurally-observable) hypothesis-identity invariant — the projection always anchors at a formation hash. Canonical vocabulary used as written: projection, hypothesis, lifecycle event, formation, promotion, demotion, dissolution, merge, split, substrate, BehavioralCluster.

- **Consequences:**
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/projection.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/projection.go) — new package + file. `State`, `LifecycleEntry`, `HypothesisProjection`, `ProjectHypothesis`, `ErrFormationNotFound`, `ErrTargetNotFormation`. ~250 lines including doc comments + the two-pass walk + the precedence rules.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/projection_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/projection_test.go) — **11 tests** covering each terminal state + precedence edges + history ordering + error paths. Imports `internal/hypothesis` (test-time only — the package is in a separate _test file and reuses the writer-side API to populate substrates for projection-side assertions; this is acceptable per the read-only-at-runtime layering choice).
  - [`services/ingestion/cmd/hypothesis-state/main.go`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/hypothesis-state/main.go) — new binary; tenth operational CLI; first read-only-classification binary.
  - [`services/ingestion/Makefile`](../../services/ingestion/Makefile) — new `hypothesis-state-build` target; help text updated.
  - [`services/ingestion/README.md`](../../services/ingestion/README.md) — new §`hypothesis-state` CLI section with state-precedence-rules explainer + scope-per-§0051 disclaimer.
  - [`docs/charter/decision-log.md`](./decision-log.md) §0051 (this entry).
  - **Test count grows.** Combined: **216 tests** across the service (up from 205 at [`§0050`](#0050--sixth-final-category-iii-lifecycle-event-behavioralclustersplit-lands-structural-inverse-of-merge-6-of-6-lifecycle-operations-now-structurally-observable-25-lifecycle-surface-complete); +11 = 11 projection tests). All passing under `go test -race ./...`.
  - **Zero external dependencies added.**
  - **Tenth operational binary lands; first read-only binary.** `cmd/` now contains ten binaries. The classification surface widens: substrate-write (six lifecycle operators + Cat II derivation = seven), substrate-audit (`verify` + `orphan-cleanup` = two), projection-read (`hypothesis-state` = one — this entry). Future projection-layer surfaces (multi-hypothesis aggregate query, projection-side caching, projection-driven inference orchestration) extend the read-only classification.
  - **§2.5 BC3 deferred-state read shape now operationally observable.** The Charter prose at §2.5 BC3 has been structurally observable since §0046 (the first lifecycle event reaching a formation), but until this entry no producer-of-the-projection existed. Operators could not ask "is hypothesis X currently promoted?" — they could only ask "what lifecycle events touch X?" and reconstruct the answer by hand. This entry closes that gap.
  - **Layering pattern established for future read-side packages.** `internal/projection` is the first package in the read-only classification; the layering choice (depend on substrate + genproto, NOT on hypothesis or other writer-side packages) is the template subsequent read-side landings will follow. The duplication of message-type discriminator constants is structurally minimal and acceptable per CLAUDE.md §7 — drift surfaces at compile time the moment either side updates a constant.
  - **Precedence rules surface as an operational convention.** The chosen `State` precedence (dissolution > split > merge > demoted > promoted > forming) is an operational convention of THIS projection, not a Charter invariant or Ontology commitment. Future projection surfaces (aggregate queries, alternative read shapes) MAY surface different precedence rules; the §2.5 BC3 + ontology contract only requires that the projection be reconstructible from the substrate — not that a unique precedence be chosen.
  - **Smoke test of binary.** Two invocations validated at commit time: (a) `bin/hypothesis-state` without `-formation-event-hash` exits 2; (b) `bin/hypothesis-state -formation-event-hash 00...00 -db /tmp/empty.db` exits 3 with `ErrFormationNotFound`.
  - **Out of scope at this layer (carry-forwards).**
    - **Multi-hypothesis aggregate queries** — "list every currently-promoted hypothesis", "every hypothesis dissolved in the last 7 days", "every merge produced by inference process X". These are projection-over-many-formations queries; the current `ProjectHypothesis` is one-formation-at-a-time. A follow-on landing introduces aggregate query surfaces if/when operational pressure surfaces them.
    - **Projection-side indexing / caching** — the on-demand linear walk is correct but cost-linear in substrate size. A materialized projection table (or per-formation index) would amortize repeated reads; deferred per the constitutional-minimalism choice above.
    - **Projection over Cat II constructs** — Category II `OperationalSession` records produced by `cmd/derive-operational-session` per [`§0043`](#0043--first-category-ii-operational-construct-lands-padded-v1-canonical-operational-definition-internalderivation--cmdderive-operational-session-introduced) have no lifecycle events (Cat II is one-shot derivation), so a projection over Cat II is structurally trivial; deferred until operator demand surfaces.
    - **Projection-driven inference orchestration** — using projection state to decide when to fire formation patterns, when to promote, when to dissolve. This is the inference-orchestration layer per [`entity-model.md` Category III](../ontology/entity-model.md); requires its own design entry and is out of scope here.
    - **Other concrete Cat III subtypes' projection** — `AutomationGroup`, `CoordinationRing`, `CampaignHypothesis` per [`entity-model.md` Category III](../ontology/entity-model.md) will each need their own lifecycle event types + projection branch. The pattern established here (per-subtype constants + per-lifecycle-event walk) is the template.
    - **Layer B deep-criterion (§2.6)** — unchanged from [`§0047`](#0047--third-category-iii-lifecycle-event-behavioralclusterdemotion-lands-promotedemote-loop-closed-0011-layer-a-cadence-gate-operationally-surfaced) carry-forward; the projection does NOT currently report evidential-independence-driven Layer B candidacy because §2.6 has not yet redacted.

- **Supersession:** None. This entry opens the read-side surface that §0045–§0050 each named as a deferred carry-forward; no prior decision reversed. Establishes a new package (`internal/projection`) + a new classification (read-only binaries) that future entries extend rather than supersede. [`§0022`](#0022--implementation-pivot-22-implementation-against-current-structural-ground-authorized-storage-technology-deferral-reversed-by-authorization) implementation-gate criteria continue to be satisfied.

## `0052` — Multi-hypothesis aggregate projection (`ListHypotheses` + `ProjectAll`); §0051 named carry-forward discharged; substrate-linear-not-quadratic walk

- **Status:** accepted.
- **Date:** 2026-05-20.

- **Context:** [`§0051`](#0051--first-projection-layer-landing-hypothesisprojection-single-hypothesis-read-side-materialization-over-the-25-lifecycle-event-chain-charter-25-bc3-deferred-state-read-shape-now-operationally-observable) landed single-hypothesis projection and named **"Multi-hypothesis aggregate queries"** as the first deferred carry-forward — operator questions like "list every currently-promoted hypothesis" or "every dissolved hypothesis in the last 7 days" require ranging over the projection of every formation. The naive composition (loop over every formation, call `ProjectHypothesis` per formation) is quadratic in substrate size: each `ProjectHypothesis` walks the full substrate, so N formations × M substrate rows = O(N·M). This entry lands a substrate-linear (O(M)) aggregate projection surface that runs a single two-pass walk regardless of formation count.

  Two structural choices decided in this entry:

  - **ProjectAll layering vs ListHypotheses convenience.** The substrate-linear walk is the structurally-meaningful primitive (`ProjectAll(ctx, sub) → map[formationHash]HypothesisProjection`); `ListHypotheses` is a thin paging/filtering wrapper on top. Both are exported because operators benefit from both (`ProjectAll` for in-process callers that already want the map keyed by hash; `ListHypotheses` for callers that want a deterministically-ordered slice with filtering/paging). The duplication is one indirection, not a constitutional one.

  - **Paging shape: Limit/Offset vs cursor-based.** Option (A): `Limit` (cap) + `Offset` (skip first N) over the deterministically-sorted projection slice. Option (B): cursor-based paging that resumes correctly across substrate growth between calls. Option (A) chosen for inception-phase posture per [`§0027`](#0027--substrate-technology-protocol-buffer-canonical-substrate-on-sqlite-blob-store-third-technology-rfc-per-0022-pivot); cursor-based paging is materially more complex (requires either an opaque cursor token whose semantics survive walk reordering, or a stable per-formation "page key" that survives the substrate-position-independent ordering chosen at §0051). Deferred until operational pressure surfaces.

- **Decision:** Land `ProjectAll` + `ListHypotheses` + `ListOptions` in `internal/projection`, with the following structural moves:

  1. **`ProjectAll(ctx, sub) (map[[32]byte]HypothesisProjection, error)`** at [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/list.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/list.go). Two-pass walk over the substrate via `substrate.WalkEvents`:
     - **Pass one:** dispatch formation + promotion rows. Initialize per-formation projection skeletons (keyed by formation event hash); build a `promotionHash → formationHash` index needed in pass two.
     - **Pass two:** dispatch demotion (resolved via the promotion-index to its formation), dissolution (targets formation directly), merge (reaches each antecedent formation), split (targets antecedent formation).
     - Sort each per-formation `LifecycleHistory` ascending by `event_time`; compute terminal `State` via the same precedence rules established at §0051 (`computeState`).

     The two-pass walk has the same structural shape as `ProjectHypothesis`'s two passes but applies them once at the substrate level rather than once per formation. Linear in substrate size (each row visited twice), independent of formation count.

  2. **`ListHypotheses(ctx, sub, opts ListOptions) ([]HypothesisProjection, error)`** at the same file. Calls `ProjectAll`, then:
     - **State filter:** drop projections whose `State` does not equal `opts.StateFilter` (empty string disables).
     - **Deterministic ordering:** ascending lex order of formation event hash. Substrate-position-independent — repeating the call against the same substrate returns projections in the same order regardless of commit order. This is the canonical "list view" ordering for inception-phase tooling.
     - **Paging:** apply `Offset` (skip first N) then `Limit` (cap returned length). Zero values disable each.

  3. **`cmd/list-hypotheses` operator interface** at [`services/ingestion/cmd/list-hypotheses/main.go`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/list-hypotheses/main.go). Eleventh operational binary; **second in the read-only classification** (alongside `hypothesis-state` from §0051). Options: `-state` (one of `forming`, `promoted`, `demoted`, `dissolved`, `merged_into`, `split_into`; empty disables); `-limit` (default 0 = unbounded); `-offset` (default 0). Structured JSON array output, one element per projection sharing the shape of `hypothesis-state`'s single-projection output. Exit codes: **0** success (including empty); **2** tool/configuration error (e.g. invalid `-state` value).

- **Constitutional review:** No Charter invariant amended. No frozen-section prose modified. Respects [§2.1](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#21-observational-integrity) — read-only over immutable substrate; no lifecycle event written, modified, or interpreted in a §2.1-violating way. Respects [§2.2](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#22-epistemic-separation) — aggregate `State` field is an operational summary across the lifecycle chain, NOT a category claim about the underlying phenomenon. Respects [§2.3](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#23-provenance-integrity) — every projection entry references its producing lifecycle event by content-hash; the aggregate projection is reconstructible from the same substrate state regardless of when or where it is computed. Respects [§2.5](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness) — projects exactly the six lifecycle operations defined at the abstract `Hypothesis` type level. Respects [§2.5 BC3](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness) — extends the BC3-mandated read shape from one-formation-at-a-time to all-formations-at-once without storing aggregate state. Respects [`§0045`](#0045--first-category-iii-hypothesis-subtype-behavioralcluster-formation-lands-25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness-structurally-observable) — every projection anchors at a formation hash. Respects [`§0051`](#0051--first-projection-layer-landing-hypothesisprojection-single-hypothesis-read-side-materialization-over-the-25-lifecycle-event-chain-charter-25-bc3-deferred-state-read-shape-now-operationally-observable) — same `State` enum, same `LifecycleEntry` shape, same precedence rules; the aggregate surface is a structural extension, not a divergence. Equivalence verified at test time (`TestListEquivalentToPerFormationProject`): per-formation projection from `ProjectAll` is byte-equal to `ProjectHypothesis(sameFormation)`. Canonical vocabulary used as written: projection, hypothesis, lifecycle event, formation, promotion, demotion, dissolution, merge, split, substrate, BehavioralCluster.

- **Consequences:**
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/list.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/list.go) — new file. `ProjectAll`, `ListHypotheses`, `ListOptions`. ~250 lines including doc comments + the two-pass walk + the filtering/paging logic.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/list_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/list_test.go) — **8 tests** covering empty substrate, mixed-state populations, state filter, ordering stability (substrate-position-independent), limit + offset paging, offset-beyond-length, ProjectAll-equivalent-to-per-formation-ProjectHypothesis (the structural-equivalence invariant), all-six-end-states aggregate stress test.
  - [`services/ingestion/cmd/list-hypotheses/main.go`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/list-hypotheses/main.go) — new binary; eleventh operational CLI; second read-only binary.
  - [`services/ingestion/Makefile`](../../services/ingestion/Makefile) — new `list-hypotheses-build` target; help text updated.
  - [`services/ingestion/README.md`](../../services/ingestion/README.md) — new §`list-hypotheses` CLI section with paging-vs-cursor scope disclaimer + linear-walk-explainer.
  - [`docs/charter/decision-log.md`](./decision-log.md) §0052 (this entry).
  - **Test count grows.** Combined: **224 tests** across the service (up from 216 at [`§0051`](#0051--first-projection-layer-landing-hypothesisprojection-single-hypothesis-read-side-materialization-over-the-25-lifecycle-event-chain-charter-25-bc3-deferred-state-read-shape-now-operationally-observable); +8 = 8 list tests). All passing under `go test -race ./...`.
  - **Zero external dependencies added.**
  - **§0051 named carry-forward discharged.** "Multi-hypothesis aggregate queries (e.g. 'list every currently-promoted hypothesis', 'every hypothesis dissolved in the last 7 days', 'every merge produced by inference process X')" — the first two examples are now directly supported via `-state` filter + paging. The third (merge-by-producer) requires additional projection state that does not yet exist (the merge event does not currently carry an "inference process" attribute); deferred along with the broader projection-driven-inference-orchestration carry-forward.
  - **Eleventh operational binary lands; second read-only binary.** `cmd/` now contains: substrate-write (7), substrate-audit/maintenance (2), projection-read (2 — `hypothesis-state` and `list-hypotheses`).
  - **Substrate-linear walk pattern established.** `ProjectAll`'s two-pass shape is the template for future aggregate read-side surfaces (e.g. cross-subtype aggregate projection once additional Cat III subtypes land). The structural lesson: any aggregate over substrate-immutable events SHOULD walk the substrate once with per-target-projection dispatch, never N times with per-target filtering — the former is linear in M (substrate size); the latter is quadratic in N·M.
  - **Equivalence invariant tested.** `TestListEquivalentToPerFormationProject` asserts that the per-formation projection from `ProjectAll` is byte-equal to `ProjectHypothesis(sameFormation)` for the same substrate state. This invariant defends against precedence-rule drift or LifecycleHistory-shape drift between the single-formation and aggregate code paths. Future projection-side optimizations (caching, incremental updates, indexing) MUST preserve this invariant.
  - **Smoke test of binary.** Two invocations validated at commit time: (a) `bin/list-hypotheses -state bogus` exits 2 with explanatory message; (b) `bin/list-hypotheses -db /tmp/empty.db` exits 0 with `[]`.
  - **Out of scope at this layer (carry-forwards).**
    - **Cursor-based paging** — Limit/Offset works for static substrate state but does not resume cleanly across substrate growth between calls (rows added between calls shift the offset semantics). Cursor paging deferred until operator pressure surfaces.
    - **Time-window filtering** — e.g. "every formation created in the last 24 hours", "every hypothesis dissolved in the last 7 days". The `LifecycleHistory` carries the timestamps; a time-window filter is straightforward to add when needed.
    - **Sort orders beyond formation-hash ascending** — e.g. by latest-event-time, by state, by promotion cadence. Multi-key sorting is straightforward to add when needed; one canonical order suffices at this layer.
    - **Aggregate counters / histograms** — "how many hypotheses are in each state", "histogram of formation-to-promotion latency". These are derived statistics over the aggregate projection; can be computed by callers from the returned list, or added as a separate read-side surface.
    - **Projection-side caching / incremental updates** — unchanged from [`§0051`](#0051--first-projection-layer-landing-hypothesisprojection-single-hypothesis-read-side-materialization-over-the-25-lifecycle-event-chain-charter-25-bc3-deferred-state-read-shape-now-operationally-observable) carry-forward.
    - **Multi-subtype aggregate** — once additional Cat III concrete subtypes land (`AutomationGroup`, `CoordinationRing`, `CampaignHypothesis`), `ProjectAll` will need a sibling per subtype, OR a generic abstract surface above the per-subtype projections. Deferred until the second concrete subtype lands.
    - **Cross-operation provenance queries** — "which merge produced this formation", "which split's antecedent contained this formation". The substrate carries the structural references; projection-side surfaces for these queries are deferred.

- **Supersession:** None. Extends the read-side surface opened at [`§0051`](#0051--first-projection-layer-landing-hypothesisprojection-single-hypothesis-read-side-materialization-over-the-25-lifecycle-event-chain-charter-25-bc3-deferred-state-read-shape-now-operationally-observable); no prior decision reversed. The equivalence invariant ensures the single-formation path (§0051) and the aggregate path (this entry) remain in structural agreement. [`§0022`](#0022--implementation-pivot-22-implementation-against-current-structural-ground-authorized-storage-technology-deferral-reversed-by-authorization) implementation-gate criteria continue to be satisfied.

## `0053` — Aggregate state counters (`CountByState` + `StateCounts`); §0052 carry-forward discharged; per-state-count equivalence invariant

- **Status:** accepted.
- **Date:** 2026-05-20.

- **Context:** [`§0052`](#0052--multi-hypothesis-aggregate-projection-listhypotheses--projectall-0051-named-carry-forward-discharged-substrate-linear-not-quadratic-walk) landed the multi-hypothesis aggregate query (`ListHypotheses`) and named **"Aggregate counters / histograms"** as a deferred carry-forward — operator questions like "how many hypotheses are in each state?" or "histogram of formation-to-promotion latency" are derived statistics over the per-formation projection. The first of those questions (per-state counts) is the smallest useful extension: an operator answering "what's the current health of the hypothesis pool?" needs total + per-state counts, not the full projection of every formation. This entry lands `CountByState` + `summarize-hypotheses` as that surface; latency histograms and other derived statistics remain follow-ons.

  One structural choice in this entry:

  - **Wire shape: sparse vs dense `by_state` map.** Option (A) — sparse: omit `by_state` keys whose value is zero. Option (B) — dense: every `State` enum value appears as a key, even at zero. Option (B) chosen: a sparse map forces consumers to distinguish "key absent" from "key present with value 0", and the distinction has no semantic content (both mean "no projections in that state"). The wire-shape predictability outweighs the few bytes saved by omission.

- **Decision:** Land `CountByState` + `StateCounts` + `summarize-hypotheses` with the following structural moves:

  1. **`StateCounts` struct** at [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/counts.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/counts.go). Two fields: `Total int` (number of formations in the substrate) and `ByState map[State]int` (per-state count; dense — every State enum value appears as a key).

  2. **`CountByState(ctx, sub) (StateCounts, error)`** at the same file. Invokes `ProjectAll` (per [`§0052`](#0052--multi-hypothesis-aggregate-projection-listhypotheses--projectall-0051-named-carry-forward-discharged-substrate-linear-not-quadratic-walk)) and aggregates the per-formation `State` values. Same substrate-linear cost as `ProjectAll` plus an O(N_formations) aggregation step over the already-materialized projection map.

  3. **`cmd/summarize-hypotheses` operator interface** at [`services/ingestion/cmd/summarize-hypotheses/main.go`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/summarize-hypotheses/main.go). Twelfth operational binary; **third in the read-only classification** (alongside `hypothesis-state` from §0051 and `list-hypotheses` from §0052). No options beyond `-db` and `-blobs`. Structured JSON output of `StateCounts`. Exit codes: **0** success (including empty substrate); **2** tool/configuration error.

  4. **Per-state-count equivalence invariant**, tested at [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/counts_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/counts_test.go) via `TestCountByStateEquivalentToListFilter`: for every State value `s`, `CountByState.ByState[s]` equals `len(ListHypotheses(ctx, sub, ListOptions{StateFilter: s}))`. This invariant defends against precedence-rule drift between the count path and the list path; both paths share `ProjectAll` so divergence would require independent post-projection logic to diverge — which the test catches at CI time.

- **Constitutional review:** No Charter invariant amended. No frozen-section prose modified. Respects [§2.1](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#21-observational-integrity) — read-only over immutable substrate; no lifecycle event written, modified, or interpreted in a §2.1-violating way. Respects [§2.2](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#22-epistemic-separation) — aggregate counts are an operational summary, NOT category claims about the underlying phenomena. Respects [§2.3](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#23-provenance-integrity) — each per-state count is reconstructible from the substrate via `ProjectAll`; no derived statistic is committed to the substrate. Respects [§2.5](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness) — aggregates exactly the six lifecycle states that §2.5 + §0045–§0050 + §0051 surface. Respects [§2.5 BC3](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness) — extends the BC3-mandated read shape with a smaller aggregate view without storing the aggregate state. Respects [`§0045`](#0045--first-category-iii-hypothesis-subtype-behavioralcluster-formation-lands-25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness-structurally-observable), [`§0051`](#0051--first-projection-layer-landing-hypothesisprojection-single-hypothesis-read-side-materialization-over-the-25-lifecycle-event-chain-charter-25-bc3-deferred-state-read-shape-now-operationally-observable), and [`§0052`](#0052--multi-hypothesis-aggregate-projection-listhypotheses--projectall-0051-named-carry-forward-discharged-substrate-linear-not-quadratic-walk) — `CountByState` is a thin aggregation on top of `ProjectAll`, sharing the same per-formation precedence rules; equivalence is tested. Canonical vocabulary used as written: projection, hypothesis, lifecycle event, formation, substrate, BehavioralCluster.

- **Consequences:**
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/counts.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/counts.go) — new file. `StateCounts`, `CountByState`. ~60 lines including doc comments.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/counts_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/counts_test.go) — **6 tests** covering empty substrate (all keys present, all zero), single-forming substrate, mixed states, all-six-end-states substrate, the per-state-count equivalence invariant against `ListHypotheses`, and the sum-equals-total structural invariant.
  - [`services/ingestion/cmd/summarize-hypotheses/main.go`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/summarize-hypotheses/main.go) — new binary; twelfth operational CLI; third read-only binary.
  - [`services/ingestion/Makefile`](../../services/ingestion/Makefile) — new `summarize-hypotheses-build` target; help text updated.
  - [`services/ingestion/README.md`](../../services/ingestion/README.md) — new §`summarize-hypotheses` CLI section with the equivalence-invariant + dense-wire-shape explainer.
  - [`docs/charter/decision-log.md`](./decision-log.md) §0053 (this entry).
  - **Test count grows.** Combined: **230 tests** across the service (up from 224 at [`§0052`](#0052--multi-hypothesis-aggregate-projection-listhypotheses--projectall-0051-named-carry-forward-discharged-substrate-linear-not-quadratic-walk); +6 = 6 counts tests). All passing under `go test -race ./...`.
  - **Zero external dependencies added.**
  - **Twelfth operational binary lands; third read-only binary.** `cmd/` now contains 12 binaries across three classifications: substrate-write (7), substrate-audit/maintenance (2), projection-read (3: `hypothesis-state`, `list-hypotheses`, `summarize-hypotheses`).
  - **§0052 named carry-forward discharged.** "Aggregate counters / histograms — 'how many hypotheses are in each state'" — directly supported. The latency-histogram example named in the same §0052 carry-forward remains follow-on (requires deriving per-formation latency statistics, which is a different shape from per-state counting).
  - **Equivalence invariant family.** Two equivalence invariants now hold across the projection layer: (1) per-formation `ProjectAll` projection byte-equal to `ProjectHypothesis(sameFormation)` (per [`§0052`](#0052--multi-hypothesis-aggregate-projection-listhypotheses--projectall-0051-named-carry-forward-discharged-substrate-linear-not-quadratic-walk)); (2) per-state count byte-equal to `len(ListHypotheses{StateFilter: state})` (this entry). Together they form a structural ladder: any future projection-layer aggregate surface MUST preserve both, and the test discipline catches drift at CI time before it lands.
  - **Smoke test of binary.** Validated at commit time: `bin/summarize-hypotheses -db /tmp/empty.db -blobs /tmp/empty` exits 0 with `{"total":0,"by_state":{"demoted":0,"dissolved":0,"forming":0,"merged_into":0,"promoted":0,"split_into":0}}`.
  - **Out of scope at this layer (carry-forwards).**
    - **Latency histograms** — derived statistics over per-formation lifecycle timestamps (e.g. formation-to-promotion duration, promotion-to-demotion duration). Requires per-formation latency extraction; structurally distinct from per-state counting. Deferred.
    - **State counts with state filter** — currently `CountByState` always returns counts for all six states. A filtered variant (e.g. "count of only the promoted hypotheses, partitioned by time window") would compose state filtering + counting. Trivial extension when needed.
    - **Time-window filters** — unchanged from [`§0052`](#0052--multi-hypothesis-aggregate-projection-listhypotheses--projectall-0051-named-carry-forward-discharged-substrate-linear-not-quadratic-walk) carry-forward.
    - **Cross-operation provenance counters** — unchanged from §0052.
    - **Projection-side caching / incremental updates** — unchanged from §0051.

- **Supersession:** None. Extends the aggregate-projection surface opened at [`§0052`](#0052--multi-hypothesis-aggregate-projection-listhypotheses--projectall-0051-named-carry-forward-discharged-substrate-linear-not-quadratic-walk); no prior decision reversed. The per-state-count equivalence invariant ensures the count path (this entry) and the list path (§0052) remain in structural agreement, the same way §0052's equivalence ensured the aggregate path and the single-formation path (§0051) stayed in agreement. [`§0022`](#0022--implementation-pivot-22-implementation-against-current-structural-ground-authorized-storage-technology-deferral-reversed-by-authorization) implementation-gate criteria continue to be satisfied.

## `0054` — Time-window filter on projection queries (latest-event semantic); §0052/§0053 carry-forward discharged; equivalence invariant preserved across the window filter

- **Status:** accepted.
- **Date:** 2026-05-20.

- **Context:** [`§0052`](#0052--multi-hypothesis-aggregate-projection-listhypotheses--projectall-0051-named-carry-forward-discharged-substrate-linear-not-quadratic-walk) and [`§0053`](#0053--aggregate-state-counters-countbystate--statecounts-0052-carry-forward-discharged-per-state-count-equivalence-invariant) each named **"Time-window filters"** as a deferred carry-forward — operator questions like "every hypothesis dissolved in the last 7 days" or "what's changed today?" require filtering the projection by a time bound. This entry adds `TimeAfterNs` + `TimeBeforeNs` to `ListOptions` and propagates the filter through both `ListHypotheses` and `CountByState`, then surfaces matching `-after-ns`/`-before-ns` options on both CLIs.

  One structural choice in this entry:

  - **Latest-event semantic vs any-event-in-window.** Option (A): window matches against the projection's LATEST event_time (the last entry in `LifecycleHistory`). Option (B): window matches if ANY event in the lifecycle history falls in the window. Option (A) chosen: operator pressure is "what's changed recently" not "what touches this window at all". A hypothesis formed 5 years ago and dissolved last week, queried with `-after-ns=<one-week-ago>`, SHOULD return under (A) — the recent change is the dissolution. Under (B) the same projection would also match for any window containing the 5-year-old formation, which is operationally noisy. Option (B) remains structurally available later if a use case surfaces (a separate `MatchAnyEvent bool` field would be additive); deferred.

- **Decision:** Land `TimeAfterNs` + `TimeBeforeNs` filtering with the following moves:

  1. **`ListOptions` extension** at [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/list.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/list.go). Two new int64 fields:
     - `TimeAfterNs` — inclusive lower bound on the latest event_time. Zero disables the lower bound.
     - `TimeBeforeNs` — inclusive upper bound on the latest event_time. Zero disables the upper bound.
     - Both bounds are INCLUSIVE per the standard half-open vs closed-window convention — the boundary value passes the filter on both sides.

  2. **`withinTimeWindow(proj, opts) bool` helper** at the same file. Pure function, no side effects. Returns true when both bounds either disabled or satisfied; defensive against empty `LifecycleHistory` (which should never occur — every projection has at least its formation entry — but the defensive branch keeps the function total).

  3. **`ListHypotheses` filter** — applies `withinTimeWindow` after the state filter and before sorting/paging.

  4. **`CountByState` signature change** — new mandatory `opts ListOptions` parameter. Honors `TimeAfterNs` + `TimeBeforeNs`. Ignores `StateFilter` (would degenerate the output to a single bucket; redundant with `len(ListHypotheses)`), `Limit`, and `Offset` (paging concerns on a sorted slice; counts reflect the full filtered population by definition). The signature change is a structural shape change to the projection API; six existing test callers revised to pass `ListOptions{}` explicitly.

  5. **`window_test.go`** at [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/window_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/window_test.go) — 7 tests:
     - Pure-formation projections in/outside window.
     - Latest-event semantic (lifecycle event AFTER formation determines the matching bound; formation-only window EXCLUDES a projection with a later lifecycle event).
     - Open lower / open upper bound behavior (zero disables that side).
     - Time-window applied to `CountByState`.
     - Inclusive boundary behavior.
     - Equivalence invariant preserved across the window filter — for every State value `s`, `CountByState.ByState[s]` STILL equals `len(ListHypotheses(opts-with-StateFilter=s))` when the same window is applied to both.

  6. **CLI surface** on both [`cmd/list-hypotheses`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/list-hypotheses/main.go) and [`cmd/summarize-hypotheses`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/summarize-hypotheses/main.go):
     - `-after-ns int64` (default 0 = no lower bound).
     - `-before-ns int64` (default 0 = no upper bound).
     - Validation: both non-negative; if both non-zero, `after-ns <= before-ns`. Invalid combinations exit 2.

- **Constitutional review:** No Charter invariant amended. No frozen-section prose modified. Respects [§2.1](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#21-observational-integrity), [§2.2](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#22-epistemic-separation), [§2.3](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#23-provenance-integrity), [§2.5](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness) — same surface as §0051/§0052/§0053; the window filter is a post-projection predicate, not a substrate-side mutation. Respects [§2.5 BC3](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness) — extends the BC3-mandated read shape with a time-window predicate without storing derived state. Respects the equivalence invariant family established at §0052 + §0053 — both invariants continue to hold when the window filter is applied to both sides. Canonical vocabulary used as written: projection, hypothesis, lifecycle event, formation, substrate.

- **Consequences:**
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/list.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/list.go) — `ListOptions` extended; new `withinTimeWindow` helper; `ListHypotheses` filter chain extended.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/counts.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/counts.go) — `CountByState` signature change (new `opts ListOptions` parameter); doc-comments updated.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/window_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/window_test.go) — **7 new tests** as enumerated above.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/counts_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/counts_test.go) — six callers revised to pass `ListOptions{}` explicitly (mechanical signature change).
  - [`services/ingestion/cmd/list-hypotheses/main.go`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/list-hypotheses/main.go) — `-after-ns` + `-before-ns` flags + validation.
  - [`services/ingestion/cmd/summarize-hypotheses/main.go`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/summarize-hypotheses/main.go) — same.
  - [`services/ingestion/README.md`](../../services/ingestion/README.md) — `list-hypotheses` + `summarize-hypotheses` sections updated with the new options + the latest-event semantic explainer.
  - [`docs/charter/decision-log.md`](./decision-log.md) §0054 (this entry).
  - **Test count grows.** Combined: **237 tests** across the service (up from 230 at [`§0053`](#0053--aggregate-state-counters-countbystate--statecounts-0052-carry-forward-discharged-per-state-count-equivalence-invariant); +7 = 7 window tests). All passing under `go test -race ./...`.
  - **Zero external dependencies added.**
  - **Two named carry-forwards discharged.** §0052's "Time-window filters" and §0053's "Time-window filters" (same name carried forward through both) are now both supported via `ListOptions.TimeAfterNs` / `TimeBeforeNs`.
  - **Signature change is non-breaking at the binary boundary.** All in-tree callers updated mechanically; the projection package has no external Go consumers yet. Future external consumers would see the new mandatory parameter as a compile-time indication at integration time.
  - **Equivalence invariant family extends.** Now applies to all `ListOptions` configurations (state filter alone, time window alone, both together) — `CountByState.ByState[s]` equals `len(ListHypotheses{StateFilter: s, TimeAfterNs: a, TimeBeforeNs: b})` for any `(a, b)` and `s`. Tested explicitly at `TestWindowFilterEquivalenceAcrossAllStates`.
  - **Latest-event semantic is the projection's first non-trivial post-projection predicate.** Earlier filters (state) collapsed the per-formation `LifecycleHistory` to a single attribute (`State`); the time-window filter is the first to consult the lifecycle history shape directly (specifically its last entry). The pattern (post-projection predicates over the materialized history) is the template subsequent richer filters will follow (per-event-type filtering, latency thresholds, etc.).
  - **Out of scope at this layer (carry-forwards).**
    - **Any-event-in-window semantic** — alternative semantic per §Context above; structurally available as an additive `MatchAnyEvent bool` field if/when a use case surfaces.
    - **Per-event-type window** — e.g. "every hypothesis whose PROMOTION fell in the last 7 days" (regardless of subsequent events). The current latest-event semantic answers "what's the latest activity?"; the per-event-type form answers "when did THIS lifecycle operation happen?". Structurally distinct; deferred.
    - **Wall-clock vs substrate-commit time semantic** — the filter currently uses `event_time` (the lifecycle event's own per-event timestamp field — `formation_at`, `promoted_at`, etc.). An alternative would be `committed_at` (substrate row's commit time). Both are valid read shapes; deferred until operator pressure surfaces.
    - **Latency histograms** — unchanged from [`§0053`](#0053--aggregate-state-counters-countbystate--statecounts-0052-carry-forward-discharged-per-state-count-equivalence-invariant) carry-forward.
    - **Cross-operation provenance queries** — unchanged from §0052/§0053 carry-forwards.

- **Supersession:** None. Extends `ListOptions` and `CountByState` opened at [`§0052`](#0052--multi-hypothesis-aggregate-projection-listhypotheses--projectall-0051-named-carry-forward-discharged-substrate-linear-not-quadratic-walk) + [`§0053`](#0053--aggregate-state-counters-countbystate--statecounts-0052-carry-forward-discharged-per-state-count-equivalence-invariant); no prior decision reversed. The `CountByState` signature change is the first projection-API shape change since §0053 introduced it; existing test callers updated mechanically. [`§0022`](#0022--implementation-pivot-22-implementation-against-current-structural-ground-authorized-storage-technology-deferral-reversed-by-authorization) implementation-gate criteria continue to be satisfied.

## `0055` — Per-projection latency derivation; §0053 latency-histogram carry-forward partially discharged at the per-projection layer

- **Status:** accepted.
- **Date:** 2026-05-20.

- **Context:** [`§0053`](#0053--aggregate-state-counters-countbystate--statecounts-0052-carry-forward-discharged-per-state-count-equivalence-invariant) named **"Latency histograms"** as a carry-forward — derived statistics over per-formation lifecycle timestamps. The histogram aggregate (buckets, percentiles) is a multi-formation aggregate; the prerequisite is per-formation latency derivation. This entry discharges the prerequisite: three per-projection latency fields are computed during `ProjectHypothesis` and `ProjectAll`, surfaced via the read-only CLIs. Histogram aggregation across many projections remains follow-on.

  One structural choice in this entry:

  - **Negative-latency handling.** A producer-supplied promotion timestamp PRECEDING the formation's `event_time` would yield a negative `formation_to_first_promotion_ns`. The substrate accepts both timestamps (operator-supplied; no temporal-ordering gate at §2.1). Option (A): clamp negative latencies to zero, treating them as "promotion was concurrent with formation". Option (B): report the raw difference, accepting that some values may be negative. Option (B) chosen per the §2.2 epistemic-separation reading — the projection reports OBSERVED timestamps, NOT a category claim about producer correctness. Clamping would be a covert category claim ("we know better than the producer"); reporting the raw value preserves the substrate's record while surfacing the anomaly for operator review.

- **Decision:** Land three per-projection latency fields with the following moves:

  1. **`HypothesisProjection` extension** at [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/projection.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/projection.go). Three new pointer-valued int64 fields:
     - `FormationToFirstPromotionLatencyNs` — elapsed ns between formation event and EARLIEST promotion. Nil when no promotion has been recorded. Per §0055 specifically the EARLIEST (not latest) — answers "how long after formation did this hypothesis first move into operational use?".
     - `LatestPromotionToLatestDemotionLatencyNs` — elapsed ns between `LatestPromotion.promoted_at` and `LatestDemotion.demoted_at`. Nil when the latest promotion has no corresponding demotion (or no promotion exists). Reuses §0051's single-projection LatestPromotion/LatestDemotion pairing semantics.
     - `FormationToDissolutionLatencyNs` — elapsed ns between formation and dissolution events. Nil when no dissolution exists.

     Pointer-valued so absent fields render as JSON null / omitempty (vs zero-valued, which would be indistinguishable from "the latency happens to be 0").

  2. **`computeLatencies(proj *HypothesisProjection)`** at [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/latency.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/latency.go). Pure function operating on a fully-populated projection — reads `LifecycleHistory` + per-type pointers; writes the three latency fields. Idempotent under repeated invocation.

  3. **Wiring into ProjectHypothesis + ProjectAll** — both call `computeLatencies` after `computeState`. Same per-projection cost; no additional substrate walks.

  4. **CLI surface** on [`cmd/hypothesis-state`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/hypothesis-state/main.go) and [`cmd/list-hypotheses`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/list-hypotheses/main.go) — JSON output gains a `latencies` object with three fields (matching the projection field names, omitempty when nil).

  5. **`latency_test.go`** at [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/latency_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/latency_test.go) — 7 tests covering: forming projection (all nil), formation-to-first-promotion populated, EARLIEST-promotion semantic (re-promotion arc: first-promotion latency uses the EARLIEST, not the latest), latest-promotion-to-latest-demotion, formation-to-dissolution, all-three-arcs-populated, ProjectAll-vs-ProjectHypothesis equivalence (extends the §0052 equivalence invariant family to the latency fields), and negative-latency-when-out-of-order (verifies the Option B raw-difference reading).

- **Constitutional review:** No Charter invariant amended. No frozen-section prose modified. Respects [§2.1](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#21-observational-integrity) — read-only computation over immutable substrate. Respects [§2.2](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#22-epistemic-separation) — latency fields report OBSERVED inter-event intervals derived from the substrate's recorded timestamps; they do NOT claim a category about producer correctness (a clamping policy would constitute such a claim). Respects [§2.3](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#23-provenance-integrity) — every latency value is reconstructible from the same substrate state via `computeLatencies`. Respects [§2.5](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness), [§2.5 BC3](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness) — latency derivation operates on lifecycle events; no substrate-side current-state record is created. Respects [`§0045`](#0045--first-category-iii-hypothesis-subtype-behavioralcluster-formation-lands-25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness-structurally-observable), [`§0051`](#0051--first-projection-layer-landing-hypothesisprojection-single-hypothesis-read-side-materialization-over-the-25-lifecycle-event-chain-charter-25-bc3-deferred-state-read-shape-now-operationally-observable), [`§0052`](#0052--multi-hypothesis-aggregate-projection-listhypotheses--projectall-0051-named-carry-forward-discharged-substrate-linear-not-quadratic-walk) — latency fields are an additive enrichment of the projection structure; the §0051 + §0052 equivalence invariants continue to hold (extended in §0055's tests). Canonical vocabulary used as written: projection, hypothesis, lifecycle event, formation, promotion, demotion, dissolution, substrate.

- **Consequences:**
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/projection.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/projection.go) — `HypothesisProjection` extended with three pointer-valued int64 fields; `ProjectHypothesis` calls `computeLatencies` after `computeState`.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/list.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/list.go) — `ProjectAll` calls `computeLatencies` per formation in the finalization loop.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/latency.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/latency.go) — new file. `computeLatencies`. ~65 lines including doc comments.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/projection/latency_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/projection/latency_test.go) — **7 new tests** as enumerated above.
  - [`services/ingestion/cmd/hypothesis-state/main.go`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/hypothesis-state/main.go) — JSON output gains `latencies` object.
  - [`services/ingestion/cmd/list-hypotheses/main.go`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/list-hypotheses/main.go) — same; each array element includes `latencies`.
  - [`services/ingestion/README.md`](../../services/ingestion/README.md) — `hypothesis-state` + `list-hypotheses` sections updated with the `latencies` field table + negative-latency explainer.
  - [`docs/charter/decision-log.md`](./decision-log.md) §0055 (this entry).
  - **Test count grows.** Combined: **244 tests** across the service (up from 237 at [`§0054`](#0054--time-window-filter-on-projection-queries-latest-event-semantic-005200053-carry-forward-discharged-equivalence-invariant-preserved-across-the-window-filter); +7 = 7 latency tests). All passing under `go test -race ./...`.
  - **Zero external dependencies added.**
  - **First per-projection enrichment beyond the immutable substrate replay.** Until this entry, every field on `HypothesisProjection` either named a specific lifecycle event (LatestPromotion, Dissolution, etc.) or summarized the chain (State). The latency fields are the first to compute DERIVED statistics — intervals between events. The pattern (pure-function derivation over an already-materialized projection) is the template for subsequent richer per-projection enrichments (e.g. cadence-gate-satisfaction-at-demotion, promotion-frequency, observation-volume per formation).
  - **§0053 latency-histogram carry-forward partially discharged.** The per-projection latency surface lands here; the histogram aggregate (bucketing, percentile computation across many projections) remains a follow-on. The §0053 carry-forward was named at the histogram level; this entry covers the prerequisite (per-projection derivation) without yet implementing the aggregate.
  - **Equivalence invariant family extends to the latency fields.** `ProjectAll[hash]` latency fields are byte-equal to `ProjectHypothesis(sameHash)` latency fields. Tested at `TestLatencyProjectAllEquivalentToProjectHypothesis`. Future projection-side optimizations MUST preserve this invariant alongside the existing State + LifecycleHistory equivalences.
  - **Negative-latency semantic is operator-visible.** A producer recording an out-of-order timestamp will produce a negative latency in the projection output; the operator can detect the anomaly and reach back to the producer. Clamping would have hidden the anomaly while changing the semantic from "observed interval" to "non-negative observed interval, with the truncation point un-recorded". The chosen semantic is more honest about substrate state.
  - **Out of scope at this layer (carry-forwards).**
    - **Histogram aggregation across projections** — buckets, percentiles, sum/count/avg over the per-projection latency fields. Discharges the §0053 carry-forward at the aggregate layer; deferred until operator pressure surfaces the bucket-shape question.
    - **Additional latency arcs** — promotion-to-dissolution (skipping demotion), demotion-to-re-promotion (cycle latency), merge-to-split (when a hypothesis is recognized as conflated soon after being recognized as merged). All structurally derivable; deferred until specific operator pressure.
    - **Wall-clock-vs-substrate-time latency** — the current fields use lifecycle event_time (`promoted_at`, `demoted_at`, etc.). An alternative would use substrate `committed_at`. Both are valid; deferred.
    - **Inference-time vs observation-time latency** — formation_at uses max(declared_at) of observations (per the canonical pattern); a separate "inference recognition latency" (formation_at − inference_started_at) is not recorded today. Deferred.
    - **Per-event-type window filter** — unchanged from [`§0054`](#0054--time-window-filter-on-projection-queries-latest-event-semantic-005200053-carry-forward-discharged-equivalence-invariant-preserved-across-the-window-filter) carry-forward.
    - **Cross-operation provenance queries** — unchanged from §0052 carry-forward.

- **Supersession:** None. Additive enrichment of `HypothesisProjection`; no prior decision reversed. The pure-function derivation pattern (`computeLatencies`) is the template for subsequent per-projection enrichments. [`§0022`](#0022--implementation-pivot-22-implementation-against-current-structural-ground-authorized-storage-technology-deferral-reversed-by-authorization) implementation-gate criteria continue to be satisfied.

## `0056` — Second Category III concrete subtype (`AutomationGroup`) formation lands; second-subtype lifecycle arc opens; typed-subtype-landings commitment reaffirmed

- **Status:** accepted.
- **Date:** 2026-05-20.

- **Context:** [`§0045`](#0045--first-category-iii-hypothesis-subtype-behavioralcluster-formation-lands-25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness-structurally-observable) opened the first Cat III concrete subtype lifecycle arc (`BehavioralCluster`); §0045–§0050 closed that arc by landing all six lifecycle operations. The §0045 commitment was that subsequent Cat III subtypes (`AutomationGroup`, `CoordinationRing`, `CampaignHypothesis` per [`entity-model.md` Category III](../ontology/entity-model.md) + [`§0010`](#0010--q2-resolution-category-iii-as-abstract-type-with-four-concrete-subtypes-behavioralcluster-coordinationring-campaignhypothesis-automationgroup-with-typed-subtype-specific-landings)) would each get their own subtype-specific landing arc — NOT a uniform abstract Cat III surface (per the §0050 reaffirmation of the typed-subtype-landings commitment). This entry begins the SECOND such arc: `AutomationGroup` formation lands here; the remaining five lifecycle operations (promotion, demotion, dissolution, merge, split for AutomationGroup) are follow-on landings.

  The subtype distinction (per [`entity-model.md`](../ontology/entity-model.md)) is constitutional, not lexical:
  - `BehavioralCluster`: actors whose patterns suggest SHARED OPERATORSHIP. Inference about WHO operates.
  - `AutomationGroup`: actors whose patterns match an AUTOMATION SIGNATURE. Inference about the operation's CHARACTER (automated, non-human).

  Two structural choices decided in this entry:

  - **Pattern interface: parallel vs generic.** Option (A) — parallel per-subtype interface: `AutomationGroupFormationPattern` returns `[]*AutomationGroupFormation` (mirrors §0045's `FormationPattern` shape exactly, with subtype-specific return type). Option (B) — generic abstract interface returning `proto.Message` or similar. Option (A) chosen per the §0045 + §0050 commitment to typed subtype-specific landings; the duplication is bounded (~150 lines per subtype: pattern interface + context + walker + a registered concrete pattern) and preferable to a generic abstraction that would invite the same kind of category-leak the Charter forbids in prose. The subtype distinction is structurally recorded by the return type itself — generic erasure would weaken that record.

  - **Group cardinality at this layer: single-actor vs multi-actor.** The canonical AutomationGroup definition is "a set of actors". Option (A) — emit one `AutomationGroupFormation` per qualifying actor (single-actor groups; sets of size 1 are valid sets). Option (B) — group qualifying actors into multi-actor formations by some similarity criterion (similar mean cadence, similar pattern parameters). Option (A) chosen at this layer per constitutional-minimalism (CLAUDE.md §7); multi-actor grouping requires a similarity metric whose choice is a separate structural commitment. Single-actor emission is structurally sound — each qualifying actor's automation-signature attribution is independently meaningful — and multi-actor grouping is straightforward to add later as a follow-on pattern (e.g. `uniform-cadence-clustered-v2`).

- **Decision:** Land `AutomationGroupFormation` as the second Cat III subtype's first lifecycle event, with four structural moves:

  1. **`AutomationGroupFormation` Protobuf message** at [`schemas/events/v1/automation_group_formation.proto`](../../schemas/events/v1/automation_group_formation.proto). Six fields mirroring §0045's `BehavioralClusterFormation` shape (`pattern_signature`, `pattern_parameters`, `actor_refs`, `formation_at`, `confidence`, `source_event_hashes`). The wire shape is identical to §0045's; the semantic distinction lives in the message_type discriminator (`ghosttrace.events.v1.AutomationGroupFormation` vs `BehavioralClusterFormation`). Per the §0045 hypothesis-identity invariant carried forward, the formation event's content-hash IS the AutomationGroup's stable identity; future AutomationGroup lifecycle events will reference it.

  2. **`FormAutomationGroupAll` + `AutomationGroupFormationPattern` interface** at [`services/ingestion/internal/hypothesis/automation_group_formation.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/hypothesis/automation_group_formation.go). Parallel to §0045's `FormAll` + `FormationPattern`; substrate walker collects `DeclaredSession` rows (the same Cat I surface BehavioralCluster patterns consume at inception; AutomationGroup patterns needing additional Cat I types — e.g. `NetworkEvent` for traffic-cadence signatures — extend the AutomationGroupFormationContext interface per the §0044/§0045 incremental-extension procedure).

  3. **`uniform-cadence-v1` formation pattern** at [`services/ingestion/internal/hypothesis/uniform_cadence_v1.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/hypothesis/uniform_cadence_v1.go). The first canonical AutomationGroup formation pattern. Algorithm: group DeclaredSessions by actor; compute the inter-event-delta sequence; emit AutomationGroupFormation per actor whose coefficient-of-variation (std-dev/mean) of deltas falls within the operator-supplied threshold. Single-actor groups per the §Context structural choice. Confidence placeholder: `1.0 - CoV/MaxCoVThreshold` (same shape as §0045's confidence placeholder pending §2.6 redaction). Determinism: byte-stable across hosts (Go's `math.Sqrt` + IEEE-754 double-precision; the threshold comparison is a single `<=` operator).

  4. **`cmd/form-automation-group` operator interface** at [`services/ingestion/cmd/form-automation-group/main.go`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/form-automation-group/main.go). Thirteenth operational binary; substrate-write classification (alongside the seven existing Cat I/II/III writers). Pattern registry currently contains only `uniform-cadence-v1`; new patterns register here.

- **Constitutional review:** No Charter invariant amended. No frozen-section prose modified. Respects [§2.1](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#21-observational-integrity) — `AutomationGroupFormation` committed under content-addressed immutability; no observation mutated. Respects [§2.2](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#22-epistemic-separation) — AutomationGroup is a Cat III hypothesis, NOT a category claim about producer identity or operation character at the substrate level. The inference is non-deterministic per §2.2 Cat III requirement; recording is deterministic. Respects [§2.3](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#23-provenance-integrity) — `source_event_hashes` references the contributing DeclaredSessions by content-hash; provenance reconstructible. Respects [§2.5](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness) — formation is the first of six lifecycle operations for this subtype; subsequent operations are follow-on landings. Respects [§2.5 BC5](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness) — the formation event IS a Cat I record under §2.1. Respects [`§0045`](#0045--first-category-iii-hypothesis-subtype-behavioralcluster-formation-lands-25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness-structurally-observable) — hypothesis identity IS the formation event's content-hash for THIS subtype too; the invariant transfers cleanly. Respects [`entity-model.md` Category III](../ontology/entity-model.md) typed-subtype-landings commitment — `AutomationGroup` is a structurally-distinct concrete subtype, NOT a label on a uniform Cat III type. Canonical vocabulary used as written: hypothesis, lifecycle event, formation, substrate, BehavioralCluster, AutomationGroup.

- **Consequences:**
  - [`schemas/events/v1/automation_group_formation.proto`](../../schemas/events/v1/automation_group_formation.proto) — new file. Six fields mirroring §0045's BehavioralClusterFormation shape; semantic distinction in the message_type discriminator.
  - [`services/ingestion/Makefile`](../../services/ingestion/Makefile) — generate target extended; new `form-automation-group-build` target.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/hypothesis/automation_group_formation.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/hypothesis/automation_group_formation.go) — new file. `AutomationGroupFormationPattern`, `AutomationGroupFormationContext`, `FormAutomationGroupAll`, `AutomationGroupReport`. Parallel to §0045's surface.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/hypothesis/uniform_cadence_v1.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/hypothesis/uniform_cadence_v1.go) — new file. `UniformCadenceV1` concrete pattern + `UniformCadenceV1Signature` constant.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/hypothesis/automation_group_formation_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/hypothesis/automation_group_formation_test.go) — **11 tests** covering happy-path, min-observation-count gate, empty-actor-ref exclusion, idempotency, versioning, threshold boundary (inclusive at equality), multiple-actor population, zero-mean defensive skip, empty substrate, nil pattern rejection, coexistence with BehavioralClusterFormation in the same substrate.
  - [`services/ingestion/cmd/form-automation-group/main.go`](../../services/ingestion/cmd/form-automation-group/main.go) — new binary; thirteenth operational CLI; substrate-write classification.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/verify/verify_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/verify/verify_test.go) — **1 new test** (`TestVerifyWithSecondCatIIISubtype`) proving verify reports success across substrates containing the second-subtype formation alongside Cat I/II rows; the substrate-integrity audit remains type-agnostic.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/canonical/corpus_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/canonical/corpus_test.go) — `messageFactory` extended with `"automation-group-formation"`.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/canonical/testdata/canonical-corpus/automation-group-formation-{minimal,typical}.{json,bin,hash}`](../../services/ingestion/internal/canonical/testdata/canonical-corpus/) — **6 new corpus files**. Mirrors §0045's Cat III formation corpus shape.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/canonical/testdata/canonical-corpus/README.md`](../../services/ingestion/internal/canonical/testdata/canonical-corpus/README.md) — Status + entries table revised to record second-subtype landing.
  - [`services/ingestion/README.md`](../../services/ingestion/README.md) — new §`form-automation-group` CLI section + lifecycle-summary paragraph updated.
  - [`docs/charter/decision-log.md`](./decision-log.md) §0056 (this entry).
  - **Test count grows.** Combined: **256 tests** across the service (up from 244 at [`§0055`](#0055--per-projection-latency-derivation-0053-latency-histogram-carry-forward-partially-discharged-at-the-per-projection-layer); +12 = 11 automation-group + 1 verify-second-subtype). All passing under `go test -race ./...`.
  - **Zero external dependencies added.**
  - **Thirteenth operational binary lands.** `cmd/` now contains 13 binaries across three classifications:
    - substrate-write (8): `form-hypothesis`, `promote-hypothesis`, `demote-hypothesis`, `dissolve-hypothesis`, `merge-hypotheses`, `split-hypothesis`, `derive-operational-session`, **`form-automation-group` (NEW)**.
    - substrate-audit/maintenance (2): `verify`, `orphan-cleanup`.
    - projection-read (3): `hypothesis-state`, `list-hypotheses`, `summarize-hypotheses`.
  - **Typed-subtype-landings commitment reaffirmed at the implementation layer.** Until §0056, the §0045 commitment ("subsequent subtypes will pursue their own subtype-specific formation patterns + lifecycle event types, NOT a generic abstract surface") had only one example. With §0056 the pattern is structurally demonstrated across two subtypes — the parallel `FormationPattern` + `AutomationGroupFormationPattern` interfaces are evidence that the commitment holds even when the wire shapes happen to be identical. Future subtypes will follow the same template.
  - **Projection layer NOT YET extended to AutomationGroup.** The §0051–§0055 projection layer (`HypothesisProjection`, `ProjectAll`, `CountByState`, time-window, latency) currently only recognizes the BehavioralCluster lifecycle event types. Projecting an AutomationGroupFormation through `ProjectHypothesis` returns `ErrTargetNotFormation` (the projection's `formationMessageType` constant is BehavioralCluster-specific). Per §0051's "Other concrete Cat III subtypes' projection" carry-forward, the projection layer needs subtype-aware code paths — either parallel (per-subtype `ProjectAutomationGroupHypothesis`) or generic (subtype-tagged). This is the natural §0057 follow-on, NOT a §0056 prerequisite.
  - **Smoke test of binary.** Validated at commit time: `bin/form-automation-group -db /tmp/empty.db -blobs /tmp/empty-blobs` exits 0 with `{"pattern_signature":"uniform-cadence-v1","pattern_parameters":"max_cov_threshold=0.15;min_observation_count=5","examined":0,"newly_formed":0,"already_formed":0}`.
  - **Out of scope at this layer (carry-forwards).**
    - **Five remaining AutomationGroup lifecycle operations** — promotion, demotion, dissolution, merge, split. Each mirrors the §0046–§0050 BehavioralCluster landings; expected to follow the same template (separately-committed formation for produced/successor identities per §0049+§0050; reusable `ErrTargetNotFound` + `ErrTargetWrongType` sentinels per §0046+§0047 generalized). Five follow-on entries.
    - **Projection layer extension for AutomationGroup** — `internal/projection` currently hard-codes BehavioralCluster message_type constants. AutomationGroup projection needs either parallel code paths or subtype-aware abstraction. Natural §0057 candidate per the above note.
    - **Multi-actor AutomationGroup formation** — single-actor groups at this layer; clustering qualifying actors by similar cadence (or other similarity metrics) is a follow-on pattern.
    - **Additional formation patterns** — `uniform-cadence-v1` is the minimum-viable canonical example. Sophisticated patterns (multi-Cat-I-input signatures, statistical fingerprinting, ensemble classifiers) extend the existing `AutomationGroupFormationPattern` pathway mechanically.
    - **Remaining Cat III subtypes** — `CoordinationRing`, `CampaignHypothesis` per [`entity-model.md` Category III](../ontology/entity-model.md). Each requires its own landing arc; `CoordinationRing` introduces pairwise-relations (new structural shape vs §0045/§0056's actor-set shape); `CampaignHypothesis` targets EVENTS not actors (most divergent shape). Deferred until operator pressure surfaces.
    - **Cross-subtype interaction (merge, split, projection)** — unchanged from [`§0049`](#0049--fifth-category-iii-lifecycle-event-behavioralclustermerge-lands-within-subtype-binary-merge-produced-hypothesis-as-separate-formation-structural-choice-5-of-6-lifecycle-operations-now-structurally-observable) + [`§0050`](#0050--sixth-final-category-iii-lifecycle-event-behavioralclustersplit-lands-structural-inverse-of-merge-6-of-6-lifecycle-operations-now-structurally-observable-25-lifecycle-surface-complete) carry-forwards. Cross-subtype merge (e.g. BehavioralCluster + AutomationGroup → ?) remains an open Ontology question per Q4 deferral.

- **Supersession:** None. Opens the second Cat III subtype lifecycle arc; no prior decision reversed. The parallel-pattern-per-subtype approach reaffirms the §0045+§0050 typed-subtype-landings commitment. [`§0022`](#0022--implementation-pivot-22-implementation-against-current-structural-ground-authorized-storage-technology-deferral-reversed-by-authorization) implementation-gate criteria continue to be satisfied.
