## `0139` — Canonical-serialization-contract revision: BLAKE3-hash-list element-shape discipline generalized from two influence-storage fields to the full canonical-form-load-bearing set

- **Status:** accepted.
- **Date:** 2026-05-22.
- **Context:** [`§0136`](#0136--canonical-serialization-contract-revision-paireddimension----graph--l-bc-or-consolidated-at-the-contract-layer-26-paireddimension-operational-discharge) canonical-serialization-contract revision named the marshalling-boundary element-shape rule for the two influence-storage fields (`closure_hashes`, `direct_influenced_by`) — 32-byte length + ascending lexicographic order + no duplicates. The §Influence Storage Validation discipline named both fields explicitly; the §Anti-Patterns entry "closure_hashes element mis-encoded" named the closure-storage field only. PR #143 operationalized the discipline at `services/ingestion/internal/canonical/canonical.go` by enforcing both fields at the marshalling boundary; PR #143's commit message explicitly flagged the deferred extension: *"Scope: only the two contract-enumerated fields. Other repeated-bytes hash fields (e.g., source_event_hashes) have similar shape requirements per their proto comments but are not contract-anti-patterns — extending validation to those would be a separate move."*

  Empirical observation across `schemas/events/v1/*.proto`: the structural discipline (32-byte BLAKE3 + ascending + dedup) is present in proto comments for FIVE field families, not two:

  | Field | Sites | Semantic surface | Proto-comment commitment |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `closure_hashes` | 4 formation protos + `OperationalSession` | Influence storage closure ([`§0134`](#0134--q5-transitivityhalf-resolution-candidate--transitive-closure-adopted-with-graph-storage-ontologymd-q5-fully-resolved-layer-b-alldependenciesdischarged) Q5-τ) | "Sorted ASCENDING lexicographic order" (§0136 §Influence Storage) |
  | `direct_influenced_by` | 4 formation protos + `OperationalSession` | Influence storage direct edges (§0134 + §0136 β-graph) | "Sorted ASCENDING lexicographic order" (§0136 §Influence Storage) |
  | `source_event_hashes` | 4 formation protos | Observational provenance roots ([§2.3](./constitutional-charter.md#23-provenance-integrity) v0.4) | "Sorted ASCENDING for content-hash stability" (each proto comment) |
  | `antecedent_formation_event_hashes` | 4 merge protos | Lifecycle merge antecedents ([§2.5](./constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness) v0.3 + [`§0045`](#0045--hypothesis-identity-formation-event-content-hash-architectural-anchor-for-cat-iii-substrate)) | "Sorted ASCENDING (byte-lexicographic) for content-hash stability — merging hypotheses A and B in either order MUST produce a byte-identical merge event" (each proto comment) |
  | `successor_formation_event_hashes` | 4 split protos | Lifecycle split successors (§2.5 v0.3 + §0045) | "Sorted ASCENDING for content-hash stability — splitting hypothesis P into successors {A, B, C} in any order MUST produce a byte-identical split event" (each proto comment) |

  Five field families share the same structural discipline (32-byte BLAKE3 + ascending + dedup) for the same reason (set-shaped reference to substrate-committed records by content-hash; substrate identity must not depend on call-order). Three of the five lack marshalling-boundary enforcement under the §0136 narrower form. The structural commitment is uniform; the contract's enforcement coverage is not.

- **Decision:** Canonical-serialization-contract revised:

  1. **New §Hash-List Field Discipline section** inserted between §Influence Storage and §Demotion-Candidacy Predicate. The section enumerates the FIVE field families subject to the uniform 32-byte BLAKE3 + ascending + dedup discipline + their semantic surfaces, names the substrate-tier validations that are supplementary to (not subsumed by) the marshalling-boundary check, and defines the scope-extension rule for future canonical-form-load-bearing hash-list fields (a new such field inherits the discipline structurally and must be added to the marshalling-boundary check at the same commit as the proto change per the §Schemas-Evolution Events boundary item 5).

  2. **§Anti-Patterns "closure_hashes element mis-encoded" renamed → "BLAKE3-hash-list element mis-encoded"** with body generalized to name all five field families. The narrower form is explicitly named as the inception-revision form (§0136) that this entry supersedes.

  3. **§Influence Storage Validation discipline clause appended** noting that the influence-storage element-shape check is the field-specific instance of the uniform Hash-List Field Discipline, and that the substrate-tier closure-recomputation check is independent of and supplementary to the marshalling-boundary check.

  4. **§References extended** with this entry as the contract-revision anchor.

  5. **Status line at top of contract refreshed** to name this entry alongside §0136 + §0138 as the third contract revision.

  The canonical/canonical.go marshalling-boundary check is extended in the same change set: `influenceHashFieldNames` (the §0136 narrower name) renamed → `hashListFieldNames`; the three field names added; doc comments + error messages updated to reflect the uniform discipline; test cases added for each new field (positive + negative).

  No Charter prose amended. The §0139 revision is contained at the canonical-serialization-contract + canonical-package layers.

- **Constitutional review:** No Charter invariant amended. The uniform structural discipline is already present in the proto comments (each of the five field families documents the ascending + content-hash-stability commitment) + already inherited from the Charter via the existing constitutional anchors:

  - `closure_hashes` + `direct_influenced_by`: [§2.4](./constitutional-charter.md#24-inferential-influence-disclosure) v0.5 + §0134 + §0136.
  - `source_event_hashes`: [§2.3](./constitutional-charter.md#23-provenance-integrity) v0.4 (provenance chain termination at Cat I; the order-stable encoding is required for content-hash stability of the formation event itself).
  - `antecedent_formation_event_hashes` + `successor_formation_event_hashes`: [§2.5](./constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness) v0.3 + §0045 (hypothesis identity IS formation hash; lifecycle event references the hypotheses by formation hash; the order-stable encoding is required for content-hash stability of the lifecycle event itself — merge/split symmetry per the proto comments).

  This entry RECOGNIZES the uniform discipline rather than CREATING new structural commitment. The §0136 narrower form was a partial expression of the same discipline; the partial expression was sufficient at PR #143 + the schemas the contract covered at the time (5 of 5 messages with influence-storage fields covered). With the proto surface having grown to include lifecycle merge/split protos (PRs #137 + #142) and the formation protos' source_event_hashes field, the same discipline applies to additional sites — three more field families covering 12 additional message types (4 merge + 4 split + 4 formation × source_event_hashes).

  Falsifiability discipline: the marshalling-boundary check is mechanically decidable on any message instance — for each named field, iterate elements, verify length=32 + ascending order + no duplicates; reject otherwise. The check produces a deterministic error message naming the field + the violation type. CI golden-file gate operating against the corpus is unaffected (existing corpus entries respect the discipline; the check accepts existing corpus + rejects new construction that violates).

  Consistent with [§4](./constitutional-charter.md#4-constitutional-design-rule) criterion 1: the canonical-serialization-contract is structural; the §0139 revision strengthens the marshalling-boundary structural enforcement without introducing operator-configurable parameters.

- **Consequences:**
  - [`docs/architecture/canonical-serialization-contract.md`](../architecture/canonical-serialization-contract.md) revised: (a) Status line refreshed with §0139 reference; (b) new §Hash-List Field Discipline section between §Influence Storage and §Demotion-Candidacy Predicate; (c) §Anti-Patterns "closure_hashes element mis-encoded" → "BLAKE3-hash-list element mis-encoded" with generalized body; (d) §Influence Storage Validation discipline clause appended; (e) §References extended.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/canonical/canonical.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/canonical/canonical.go) revised: `influenceHashFieldNames` → `hashListFieldNames`; three field names added (`source_event_hashes`, `antecedent_formation_event_hashes`, `successor_formation_event_hashes`); doc comments + error messages updated.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/canonical/canonical_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/canonical/canonical_test.go) extended: positive + negative test cases per new field family (length mismatch + descending order + duplicate per field).
  - CI golden-file gate unaffected — existing corpus entries respect the discipline at every site (verified before the revision committed). Schemas-Evolution Events boundary NOT triggered for this change: the .proto files are unchanged; the canonical-serialization library's behavior on existing well-formed inputs is unchanged; only the rejection-set for malformed inputs expands. Per the contract's §Schemas-Evolution Events boundary item 5 ("Any `.proto` file's structural commitments change"), this revision does not qualify — the .proto file commitments are unchanged; the change is at the marshalling-pipeline-rejection layer only.
  - **§0136 narrower form superseded.** The §0136 §Anti-Patterns "closure_hashes element mis-encoded" entry is renamed + generalized; the §0136 §Influence Storage Validation discipline is preserved and supplemented (the field-specific clause remains; a cross-reference to the new §Hash-List Field Discipline section is added).
  - **Methodological observation 1 — Patch-via-pressure pattern fifth instance; second proto-layer instance.** Pattern catalogue: [`§0018`](#0018--fix-frozen-section-parser-to-accept-amendmentqualified-status-cells-v041) (v0.4.1 parser fix) → [`§0100`](#0100--frozennewly-frozen-section-exemption--amendment-in-progress-exemption-v051--v052) (v0.5.1 hook fix) → [`§0101`](#0101--252--bc5-prose-reformulation-with-hook-amendmentinprogress-exemption-v052) (v0.5.2 hook extension + BC5 reformulation) → [`§0137`](#0137--patch-amendment-v071-charter-26--3-0034--0136-staleanchor-correction-0136-anchorfidelity-observation-discharged) (v0.7.1 Charter cross-reference) → this entry (canonical-serialization-contract uniform-discipline generalization). The §0137 narrative observation 3 (anchor-fidelity verification as Step 1.1 augmentation) extended naturally to this case: the §0136 contract revision committed coverage at the then-extant surface (2 fields); subsequent proto-layer evolution (PRs #137 + #142 introducing 12 additional sites with the same structural commitment) surfaced the coverage gap. **Future contract revisions should explicitly cross-reference the canonical-form-load-bearing proto surface at the time of revision; later proto additions may surface uniform-discipline applicability gaps that warrant catch-up revisions per this precedent.**
  - **Methodological observation 2 — Uniform-discipline recognition vs new-commitment introduction.** This entry RECOGNIZES a uniform discipline already present in the proto comments + already inherited from the Charter via the existing constitutional anchors (§2.3 + §2.4 + §2.5); it does NOT introduce new structural commitment. The Charter is unchanged; the canonical-serialization-contract is RECOGNIZING what was already true at the constitutional layer + crystallizing the marshalling-boundary enforcement coverage. **Distinguishing recognition from introduction is methodologically important: recognition operates under the contract's existing structural surface; introduction would require a new constitutional anchor.** Future canonical-serialization-contract revisions should explicitly label themselves as recognition vs introduction per this precedent.
  - **Methodological observation 3 — Marshalling-boundary check coverage now uniform across the BLAKE3-hash-list surface.** Pre-§0139: 2 of 5 hash-list field families enforced at the marshalling boundary (closure_hashes + direct_influenced_by). Post-§0139: 5 of 5 enforced. The substrate-tier validations (closure-recomputation per Cat II transmission; provenance-chain termination at Cat I; merge/split structural symmetry) remain follow-on per the contract's discipline of distinguishing field-shape (marshalling boundary) from substrate-state (substrate commit-time). **The coverage symmetry is now a contract-layer invariant; future canonical-form-load-bearing hash-list fields must inherit the marshalling-boundary check at the same commit as their proto introduction.**

- **Supersession:** [`§0136`](#0136--canonical-serialization-contract-revision-paireddimension----graph--l-bc-or-consolidated-at-the-contract-layer-26-paireddimension-operational-discharge) inception-revision §Anti-Patterns entry name + body superseded by the generalized form at this entry; the §0136 §Influence Storage Validation discipline is preserved + supplemented (not superseded). No other prior entry superseded.

## `0140` — Canonical-serialization-contract revision: paired-dimension marshalling-boundary enforcement corrected (`AllowPartial: false` no-op for proto3 acknowledged; explicit canonical-package check installed)

- **Status:** accepted.
- **Date:** 2026-05-23.
- **Context:** [`§0136`](#0136--canonical-serialization-contract-revision-paireddimension----graph--l-bc-or-consolidated-at-the-contract-layer-26-paireddimension-operational-discharge) canonical-serialization-contract revision consolidated the paired-dimension commitment at the contract layer per [§2.6](./constitutional-charter.md#26-evidential-independence-integrity) v0.6 operational discharge. The §Paired-Dimension Commitment §Required fields paragraph claimed: *"Both fields are required (`AllowPartial: false` in the canonical Marshal call rejects records missing either)."* The §Validation discipline paragraph claimed: *"Substrate-commit fails at the canonical-marshalling boundary when a record subject to the commitment is missing either dimension."*

  Empirical assessment surfaces a structural inconsistency between two sites of the same contract: the §Marshal call section (line 62 in v0.7.1 of the contract) explicitly acknowledges that `AllowPartial: false` is structurally a no-op for proto3 — *"proto3 has no required fields per se, but `AllowPartial: false` preserves the discipline boundary in case proto2-derived types ever appear in the codebase."* The §Paired-Dimension Commitment paragraph relies on the option as if it were enforcing; the §Marshal call section says it is not.

  The empirical evidence at the canonical-package layer is unambiguous: a record subject to the paired-dimension commitment (`BehavioralClusterFormation` and its three sibling Cat III formation protos + `OperationalSession`) committed with `confidence` set but `evidential_independence` left as the nil message default passed `Marshal()` without rejection. The pre-§0140 canonical-package test `TestMarshalAcceptsUnsetEvidentialIndependence` explicitly codified this — its body asserted exactly that the bypass succeeds, with the comment *"Paired-dimension presence-enforcement is a substrate-tier concern per the canonical-serialization-contract"* — directly contradicting the contract's §Validation discipline claim of marshalling-boundary enforcement.

  Worse: the canonical-corpus golden-file gate had ten entries (4 × formation-{minimal, typical} + behavioral-cluster-formation-shared-descriptor + operational-session-{minimal, padded-v1}) that committed paired-dimension subject records WITHOUT `evidential_independence` populated. The pre-§0140 corpus was, in effect, a golden-file record of the §2.6 v0.6 anti-pattern 1 (paired-dimension bypass) being committed as accepted-canonical behavior. The contract's claimed operational discharge of §2.6 was undischarged at the runtime layer; only the type-definition layer (both fields are DECLARED in every paired-dimension subject proto) was discharged.

- **Decision:** Canonical-serialization-contract revised + canonical-package extended + corpus brought into compliance:

  1. **§Paired-Dimension Commitment §Required fields paragraph rewritten.** The structurally-incorrect `AllowPartial: false` claim is removed; the canonical-package check (`validatePairedDimensionCommitment`) is named as the actual enforcement mechanism; the asymmetric design is documented (EI presence enforced; confidence presence not enforced — proto3 scalar with no field-presence; `confidence = 0.0` is a valid low-confidence commitment). The §Marshal call section's `AllowPartial: false` description is repositioned in the paragraph as a defense-in-depth boundary for proto2-derived types, not as the proto3 enforcement mechanism.

  2. **§Paired-Dimension Commitment §Validation discipline paragraph clarified.** The failure mode is named precisely: *"records subject to the commitment with `evidential_independence` absent at commit time"* (asymmetric); cross-reference to the rational-pair validation (the existing `validateEvidentialIndependence` walker) as supplementary, not subsumed.

  3. **§Anti-Patterns "Paired-dimension bypass" entry revised.** The detection mechanism is updated from the structurally-incorrect `AllowPartial: false` reference to the explicit canonical-package check; the asymmetric scope (EI absence only) is named; confidence-presence exclusion is documented.

  4. **§References extended** with this entry as the third contract-revision anchor.

  5. **Status line at top of contract refreshed** to name this entry alongside §0136 + §0138 + §0139 as the fourth contract revision.

  The canonical-package change set:

  - [`services/ingestion/internal/canonical/canonical.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/canonical/canonical.go) extended: `validatePairedDimensionCommitment` added; wired as the third marshalling-boundary validator (after `validateHashListFields` + `validateEvidentialIndependence`); rejects records that declare BOTH `confidence` + `evidential_independence` field names but have `evidential_independence` absent at commit time. Asymmetric design documented inline.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/canonical/canonical_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/canonical/canonical_test.go) revised: pre-§0140 `TestMarshalAcceptsUnsetEvidentialIndependence` renamed → `TestMarshalRejectsUnsetEvidentialIndependence` with assertion inverted + comment rewritten to anchor §0140; two existing positive-path tests (`TestMarshalAcceptsWellFormedClosureHashes`, `TestMarshalAcceptsWellFormedSourceEventHashes`) extended to set `EvidentialIndependence` on their `BehavioralClusterFormation` fixtures (the fixtures previously slipped through under the missing enforcement; with §0140 active, they must include EI).
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/canonical/coverage_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/canonical/coverage_test.go) extended: `TestPairedDimensionSubjectSet_StructuralDetection` added; asserts the structural detection used by `validatePairedDimensionCommitment` ("declares both confidence + evidential_independence fields") selects exactly the contract-enumerated paired-dimension subject set (4 formation protos + OperationalSession). Mechanizes drift protection — a future proto change that adds OR removes one of the paired-dimension fields surfaces at the same commit.
  - Ten corpus entries updated to include `evidentialIndependence` per §0140 compliance: 4 × `<subtype>-formation-minimal.json` (added `{numerator: 0, denominator: 1}` — minimum-valid α = 0); 4 × `<subtype>-formation-typical.json` (added meaningful α values: AG = 2/3, BC-shared-descriptor = 1/2, CH = 2/3, CR = 1/3); `operational-session-minimal.json` (added α = 0); `operational-session-padded-v1.json` (added α = 1, full independence). Golden `.bin` + `.hash` files regenerated for all ten entries via `go test -run TestCanonicalCorpus -update`.

  This change set is a **schemas-evolution event** per the contract's §Schemas-Evolution Events boundary item 9 (*"paired-dimension required-fields shape changes — which record types are subject to the commitment, which fields are required, validation discipline"*). The contract's validation discipline IS changing (from claim-only to runtime-enforced); the goldens MUST regenerate; the regeneration is committed alongside this entry.

- **Constitutional review:** No Charter invariant amended. The §2.6 v0.6 anti-pattern 1 (paired-dimension bypass) was already in force at the Charter layer; §0140 brings the contract's operational discharge into structural agreement with the Charter's commitment by replacing the stale `AllowPartial: false` mechanism with the actual enforcement mechanism. Bidirectional reinforcement with [§2.6 frozen v0.6](./constitutional-charter.md#26-evidential-independence-integrity) is strengthened — the anti-pattern is now operationally enforced, not just structurally declared.

  Falsifiability discipline: the new check is mechanically decidable on any message instance — for each message type with `confidence` + `evidential_independence` declared, examine `m.Has(eiFd)` at marshalling boundary; reject if false. The check produces a deterministic error message naming the message type + the §0140 anchor.

  Consistent with [§4](./constitutional-charter.md#4-constitutional-design-rule) criterion 1: the canonical-serialization-contract is structural; the §0140 revision strengthens marshalling-boundary structural enforcement without introducing operator-configurable parameters. Asymmetric enforcement (EI required; confidence not enforced) is structurally justified — proto3 scalar fields lack field-presence; `confidence = 0.0` is a valid semantic commitment; absence of `evidential_independence` is a structural commitment violation under §2.6.

  Consistent with [§2.6](./constitutional-charter.md#26-evidential-independence-integrity) anti-pattern 1: the bypass detection mechanism advances from claim ("`AllowPartial: false` rejects missing required fields") to operational discharge (`validatePairedDimensionCommitment` rejects EI-absent commits).

- **Consequences:**
  - [`docs/architecture/canonical-serialization-contract.md`](../architecture/canonical-serialization-contract.md) revised: (a) Status line refreshed with §0140 reference; (b) §Paired-Dimension Commitment §Required fields paragraph rewritten with asymmetric-enforcement documentation; (c) §Paired-Dimension Commitment §Validation discipline paragraph clarified; (d) §Anti-Patterns "Paired-dimension bypass" entry detection-mechanism updated; (e) §References extended.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/canonical/canonical.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/canonical/canonical.go) extended with `validatePairedDimensionCommitment` + wired into `Marshal()`.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/canonical/canonical_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/canonical/canonical_test.go) revised: test inversion + fixture extensions per §0140 compliance.
  - [`services/ingestion/internal/canonical/coverage_test.go`](../../services/ingestion/internal/canonical/coverage_test.go) extended with `TestPairedDimensionSubjectSet_StructuralDetection` + `pairedDimensionSubjectSet` allowlist.
  - 10 corpus JSON entries updated; 10 corresponding `.bin` + `.hash` goldens regenerated.
  - **CI golden-file gate behavior**: existing well-formed inputs whose canonical bytes are unchanged remain accepted (no change to the canonical-serialization algorithm; only the rejection-set for paired-dimension-subject records with absent EI expands). The 10 corpus entries' canonical bytes DO change because their JSON sources change (added EI field); the goldens regenerate accordingly.
  - **Methodological observation 1 — Patch-via-pressure pattern sixth instance; second canonical-package-layer instance; first instance surfacing an INTERNAL contradiction between two sites of the same contract.** Pattern catalogue: [`§0018`](#0018--fix-frozen-section-parser-to-accept-amendmentqualified-status-cells-v041) → [`§0100`](#0100--frozennewly-frozen-section-exemption--amendment-in-progress-exemption-v051--v052) → [`§0101`](#0101--252--bc5-prose-reformulation-with-hook-amendmentinprogress-exemption-v052) → [`§0137`](#0137--patch-amendment-v071-charter-26--3-0034--0136-staleanchor-correction-0136-anchorfidelity-observation-discharged) → [`§0139`](#0139--canonical-serialization-contract-revision-blake3-hash-list-element-shape-discipline-generalized-from-two-influence-storage-fields-to-the-full-canonical-form-load-bearing-set) → this entry. Prior instances surfaced gaps between distinct documents (hook vs Charter; canonical-package vs proto comments); this entry surfaces a gap between two paragraphs of the SAME contract document. **Future contract authorship should explicitly cross-check claims about enforcement mechanisms against the §Marshal call section's structural-truth statements (proto3-no-required, etc.) at the same commit; the §Paired-Dimension Commitment paragraph's pre-§0140 form was authored without re-reading the §Marshal call section's acknowledgement that `AllowPartial: false` is a no-op for proto3.**
  - **Methodological observation 2 — Asymmetric enforcement is structurally justified, not a discipline compromise.** The §0140 enforcement enforces EI presence but not confidence presence. The asymmetry tracks the proto3 type-system: `evidential_independence` is a message field (has presence); `confidence` is a scalar field (no presence; default-value `0.0` is structurally indistinguishable from "not set"). The structural failure mode the commitment defends against is *confidence-without-EI* — an inferential record committed without its EI dimension. *EI-without-confidence* is not a structural failure mode for records subject to the commitment because (a) the records declare both fields by construction at the proto layer, and (b) confidence's zero-value is semantically meaningful (low-confidence commitment, not an absence). **Future enforcement choices on proto3 message/scalar field pairs should consider the asymmetry structurally rather than seeking symmetric enforcement at the cost of conflating "not set" with "set to zero."**
  - **Methodological observation 3 — Golden-file corpus as silent-bypass evidence.** The pre-§0140 corpus contained ten entries committed without EI on paired-dimension subject types; the golden files (.bin + .hash) had captured the canonical bytes of EI-absent records as accepted-canonical. The corpus was, in effect, archaeological evidence that the §2.6 v0.6 anti-pattern 1 had been silently bypassed since §0136's claimed operational discharge. **Future corpus authorship should explicitly include EI on paired-dimension subject types as part of the "minimum valid record" definition; the §0140 corpus revision establishes this precedent for all future formation/OperationalSession entries.**

- **Supersession:** [`§0136`](#0136--canonical-serialization-contract-revision-paireddimension----graph--l-bc-or-consolidated-at-the-contract-layer-26-paireddimension-operational-discharge) §Paired-Dimension Commitment §Required fields claim (re `AllowPartial: false` enforcement) superseded by the explicit-canonical-package-check form at this entry. The §0136 §Paired-Dimension Commitment §Records subject to the commitment enumeration is preserved + cross-referenced (not superseded). No other prior entry superseded.

## `0141` — Layer B service-tier implementation resolution: conservative-defaults bundle adopted (A1 internal-package + B1 on-the-fly + C1 substrate-global + D1 transient-DemoteReport + E1 advisory-like-Layer-A + F3 CLI-operator-supplied-with-bundled-defaults)

- **Status:** accepted.
- **Date:** 2026-05-23.

The §0136 + §0140 canonical-serialization-contract is consumed (read at runtime by the implementation), not modified.   Falsifiability discipline: the Evaluate function's behavior is mechanically observable via unit tests over fixture substrate state; outputs (`Verdict` shape) are deterministic given inputs.

  Consistent with [§1 Thesis](./constitutional-charter.md#1-thesis): the advisory pattern (E1) preserves operator authority over substrate commits while surfacing Layer B's structural defense state. Consistent with [§4 criterion 1](./constitutional-charter.md#4-constitutional-design-rule): the implementation is structurally enforceable; the parameters are operator-supplied at promote time (per F3) with substrate-grounded defaults.

The three-phase methodology (framing → substantive → resolution) was first instantiated at structural RFCs; extended to operational-spec at contract layer at [`§0138`](#0138--layer-b-parameter-calibration-resolution-inceptionphase-values-fixed-tb05-kc05-n1000-wcount-uuniform-na1-day-bundled-perparameter-reversalconditions); this entry extends it to operational-spec at service tier. **Future service-tier RFCs may adopt the three-phase pattern with the lighter Phase 3 per the operational-spec precedent.**
  - **Methodological observation 2 — Sub-decision structural-preclusion detectable at Phase 3 via canonical-serialization-contract re-reading.** Per evidence Phase 3 primary finding: sub-decision C was over-framed in Phase 2 (4 candidates); the contract's `§Demotion-Candidacy Predicate` section explicitly determines the window stream as substrate-global. The framing-PR over-enumeration was detectable only at Phase 3 by re-reading the contract. Pattern parallel to T_B-derived structural-preclusion from [`§0138`](#0138--layer-b-parameter-calibration-resolution-inceptionphase-values-fixed-tb05-kc05-n1000-wcount-uuniform-na1-day-bundled-perparameter-reversalconditions) Phase 3 sub-decision 1, but at implementation tier rather than parameter tier. **Future operational-spec RFCs should re-check the canonical-serialization-contract for structural determination of each sub-decision before Phase 3 begins.**
  - **Methodological observation 3 — Predecessor-decision inheritance conflict detectable at Phase 3 via epistemic-separator.** Per evidence Phase 3 tertiary finding: F2 (separate Layer A config) reverses [`§0138`](#0138--layer-b-parameter-calibration-resolution-inceptionphase-values-fixed-tb05-kc05-n1000-wcount-uuniform-na1-day-bundled-perparameter-reversalconditions) bundling. The inheritance conflict was visible only by reading the predecessor decision-log entry. **Future operational-spec RFCs should explicitly inventory predecessor committee decisions during Phase 1 to avoid framing candidates that revisit them.**
  - **Methodological observation 4 — Conservative-defaults bundle inheritance from Layer A pattern is a recurring service-tier pattern.** Per evidence Phase 4 Finding 3: the conservative-defaults bundle A1 + B1 + D1 + E1 inherits the existing Layer A handling pattern at the service tier exactly. Layer A is computed on-the-fly (no projection); the verdict is transient (in DemoteReport, not substrate-committed); it's advisory (demote records regardless); it lives in an internal package. Adopting the same pattern for Layer B inherits the established service-tier discipline. **Future service-tier RFCs adding new evaluations to existing CLIs should consider inheriting the Layer A pattern as the inception-phase default; reversal triggers name what would break the inheritance.**

- **Supersession:** None. Completes the Layer B operational arc at the service-tier layer. - **Status:** accepted.

  Each affected BC's binding commitment ("§X does not govern Y formal specifics") is independent of which entry the formal mechanism is anchored to — the stale anchors were status-reporting drift, not enforcement-relevant. The patch consolidates the seven corrections into a single amendment per the [`§0137`](#0137--patch-amendment-v071-charter-26--3-0034--0136-staleanchor-correction-0136-anchorfidelity-observation-discharged) Methodological observation 2 (bundle-by-shape) precedent: shared pattern shape (stale Q-pending anchor) + shared correction shape (replace with resolved-at-§NNNN reference + preserve BC binding text verbatim).

  Pattern instance: **fourth occurrence of the patch-via-pressure pattern at the Charter level**, and **first deliberate enaction** of the pattern rather than incidental observation. Prior three instances all surfaced from downstream incidental observation: [`§0018`](#0018--fix-frozen-section-parser-to-accept-amendmentqualified-status-cells-v041) (v0.4.1 parser fix, surfaced at §2.5 freeze self-test discrepancy), [`§0100`](#0100--frozennewly-frozen-section-exemption--amendment-in-progress-exemption-v051--v052) (v0.5.1 hook extension, surfaced at §2.4 freeze pending→frozen promotion), [`§0137`](#0137--patch-amendment-v071-charter-26--3-0034--0136-staleanchor-correction-0136-anchorfidelity-observation-discharged) (v0.7.1 Charter cross-references, surfaced at §0136 contract revision).   - §2.6 BC5 (L279): Q2 stale anchor → `§0023` reference + multi-tier deferral noted.

  The Charter banner version line advances `v0.7.1` → `v0.7.2` with a patch clause appended. The [`amendments.md` v0.7.2 entry](../charter/amendments.md) records the patch with `**Sections affected:**` line naming §2.3 + §2.4 + §2.6 (per the hook's amendment-in-progress exemption from [v0.5.2](../charter/amendments.md#v052--hook-amendment-in-progress-exemption--23-bc5-vocabulary-tightening)). CLAUDE.md §4 status table narrative paragraph appends a v0.7.2 clause per [`§0017`](#0017--gate-23-second-objectlevel-invariant-redaction-path-a-full-redaction-amendment-v04) + [`§0022`](#0022--implementation-pivot-64-amendment--0003-reversal-authorization--2426-posture-shift) + [`§0137`](#0137--patch-amendment-v071-charter-26--3-0034--0136-staleanchor-correction-0136-anchorfidelity-observation-discharged) precedent.

Per [v0.4.1](../charter/amendments.md#v041--fix-frozen-section-parser-to-accept-amendment-qualified-status-cells) / [v0.5.1](../charter/amendments.md#v051--hook-fix-handle-pendingfrozen-promotion-prs-no-charter-prose-amended) / [v0.7.1](../charter/amendments.md#v071--fix-26--3-stale-anchor-0034--0136-canonical-serialization-contract-paired-dimension-enforcement) precedent, patch-level amendments preserving Charter semantics qualify under the `amendments.md` §Amendment Discipline patch rules.

The patch is mechanically verifiable via diff inspection.

- **Consequences:**
  - Charter §2.3 + §2.4 + §2.6 prose corrected at seven cross-reference sites. Charter version advances `v0.7.1` → `v0.7.2`.
  - [`amendments.md` v0.7.2 entry](../charter/amendments.md) records the patch with full Summary + Rationale + Falsifiability review outcome subsections per the v0.4.1 / v0.5.1 / v0.5.2 / v0.7.1 precedent.
  - CLAUDE.md §4 status table narrative paragraph extends with v0.7.2 clause.
  - [`docs/rfcs/draft/charter-amendment-v0-7-2-stale-anchor-sweep.md`](../rfcs/draft/charter-amendment-v0-7-2-stale-anchor-sweep.md) is the originating RFC for this patch; status `accepted`.
  - **[`§0137`](#0137--patch-amendment-v071-charter-26--3-0034--0136-staleanchor-correction-0136-anchorfidelity-observation-discharged) Methodological observation 3 first deliberate enaction.** The anchor-inventory checklist that §0137 prescribed for future §-section redactions is exercised here for the first time as a deliberate sweep rather than an incidental observation. This validates the prescription as operationally tractable.
  - **Methodological observation 1 — Patch-via-pressure pattern at four instances; pattern shape now includes multi-anchor (heterogeneous) sweeps.** Prior three instances were homogeneous: §0018 was one regex fix; §0100 was one hook extension (with two sub-changes bundled per v0.5.1+v0.5.2); §0137 was six occurrences of the same `§0034 → §0136` swap. This entry is the first heterogeneous sweep — three different Q-resolutions (Q2 + Q3 + Q5) at seven sites — bundled under the [v0.7.1](../charter/amendments.md#v071--fix-26--3-stale-anchor-0034--0136-canonical-serialization-contract-paired-dimension-enforcement) Methodological observation 2 bundle-by-shape rationale: same pattern shape (stale Q-pending) + same correction shape (resolved-at-§NNNN reference). **Future patches may bundle heterogeneous corrections when shape uniformity holds.**
  - **Methodological observation 2 — Deliberate inventory yields different pattern of findings than incidental observation.** Incidental observation (prior three instances) surfaces single-anchor issues at the moment they bite. Deliberate inventory (this instance) surfaces aggregate stale-anchor sets that accumulated silently across multiple freezes. The two methods are complementary: deliberate inventory should be invoked before any new RFC framing that will cite Charter BCs; incidental observation continues to catch issues that deliberate inventory missed. **Future Domain Pack RFCs and any RFC citing multiple Charter BCs should trigger deliberate inventory first.**
  - **Methodological observation 3 — Anchor inventory should be extended to subordinate documents during deliberate sweeps.** The scan that surfaced these seven anchors checked only Charter prose. Subordinate documents (Ontology, Architecture, RFCs in `accepted` or `draft` status) may carry stale anchors of the same shape. The scan was extended to `docs/architecture/`, `docs/ontology/`, `docs/rfcs/` during pre-patch verification and found no architecture-layer stale anchors and only historical references in RFCs/discussion scratches (preserved by design as records of state at proposal time). **Future deliberate sweeps should extend the scan to subordinate documents and explicitly distinguish (a) stale anchors in current binding text from (b) historical references in immutable records.**

- **Supersession:** No prior decision-log entry superseded. First deliberate enaction of [`§0137`](#0137--patch-amendment-v071-charter-26--3-0034--0136-staleanchor-correction-0136-anchorfidelity-observation-discharged) Methodological observation 3 (anchor-inventory checklist).

cross-subtype framework closed ([`§0122`](#0122--crosssubtype-merge-typing-resolution-candidate--perpair-canonicalmerge-typing-formadopt--tabledefer)–[`§0127`](#0127--crosssubtype-merge-attachmentmechanism-resolution-candidate--separatelycommitted-attachment-record)); technology selections accepted (proto3 schemas; storage tiers; HTTP auth model; Go implementation language).

- **Decision:** Framing PR accepted. The RFC opens as a new category — **domain-pack** — distinct from `ontology-revision`, `operational-spec`, `architecture`, and `charter-amendment`. Structure is hybrid: constitutional framing per `ontology-revision-*` precedent (postura + tese + Q1–Q6 review + anticipated OMQs) + executable criterion per `operational-spec-*` precedent (falsifiable sub-benchmarks + instrumentation specification + milestone ordering + assumptions named explicitly).

  Scope: **Camada 1** of the cross-Claude landscape mapping (F1 typed observation taxonomy + F2 Cat II library + F3 signature engines + F4 authentication-class typing) **plus F6** (operator-grade explainability as architecture, not UX) from Camada 2. Out-of-scope: F5 (real-time decisioning), F7 (broader adversarial workflows), F8 (privacy), F9 (cross-tenant), F10 (performance/scale).

  Comprovation criterion: **two falsifiable sub-benchmarks**. Sub-benchmark 1 (month 3–4): first non-trivial demotion under public + synthetic sources. Sub-benchmark 2 (month 5–6): first non-trivial demotion under honeypot (non-curated). Non-trivial = non-tautological (signature did not encode its own demotion criterion) + provenance reconstructible + Layer A + Layer B substrate-grounded. **Mandatory instrumentation per subtype × fonte × morfologia-de-chain** wired from build time (marshalling-boundary constraint, not retroactive add-on). The diagnostic distinction between chains-fracas (depth ≤ 2 OR breadth-at-root ≤ 3 indicating F3 insufficient) vs chains-fortes with EI stable (indicating constitutional thesis confirmed — domain rotates evidence faster than decay) requires the morphology dimension at instrumentation, not at analysis.

  Anticipated OMQs (five structural pressures expected during F1–F6 build): three on existing OMQ surfaces (provenance-model.md OMQ #1 granularity-of-derivation; lifecycle-semantics.md OMQs for op-def-versioning + cross-category-lifecycle-interactions); **two NEW requiring registration** in [`entity-model.md` OMQ section](../ontology/entity-model.md#open-modeling-questions) via separate ontology-revision RFCs proposed for opening when triggered: (a) phenomenon-vs-record reconciliation under multi-source ingestion (trigger: F1 has two sources stable); (b) authentication-class typing (trigger: F1 has three modalities stable). Cross-domain provenance OMQ (provenance-model.md OMQ #4) is explicitly out-of-scope.

  Assumptions explicitly named (load-bearing for criterion falsifiability): single-developer baseline capacity (non-firing under capacity < baseline is uninformative); brand-jurisdiction honeypot legal-review (4–6 weeks; EU-post-GDPR pushes Sub-benchmark 2 by ~4 weeks); Charter stability during the window (patch amendments tolerated, §-section amendments require RFC re-baseline); decision-log empirical-pressure discipline (every constitutional pressure surfaced is captured per [`§0022`](#0022--implementation-pivot-64-amendment--0003-reversal-authorization--2426-posture-shift) methodology).

- **Constitutional review:** No Charter prose modified. The RFC consumes Charter v0.7.2 frozen state as given. Each invariant is consumed but not modified: §2.1 (Cat I substrate immutability inherited by F1 observations + F3 formation events per [§2.5 BC](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#25-hypothesis-lifecycle-explicitness)); §2.2 (Cat II constructs derived under versioned operational definitions per Q1 determinism); §2.3 (provenance chains terminate at Cat I primaries — F1 are the termini); §2.4 (F3 declares `influenced_by` at formation event time per §2.4 BC3 substrate-time generation per [`§0021`](#0021--ontology-modeling-question-3-influence-at-projection-vs-substrate-cascadetriggered-from-omq-2-resolution-2-1)); §2.5 (lifecycle events for F3-formed hypotheses are Cat I records subject to §2.5); §2.6 (F3 commits `evidential_independence` at formation per [`§0136`](#0136--canonical-serialization-contract-revision-paireddimension----graph--l-bc-or-consolidated-at-the-contract-layer-26-paireddimension-operational-discharge) canonical-serialization-contract + [`§0140`](#0140--canonical-serialization-contract-revision-paireddimension-marshallingboundary-enforcement-corrected-allowpartial-false-no-op-for-proto3-acknowledged-explicit-canonical-package-check-installed) marshalling-boundary enforcement; EI rule per [`§0133`](#0133--q3-resolution-candidate--sourcecount-ratio-adopted-26-bc1-operational-specification-discharged-0132-cascade-trigger-fires-q5-transitivityhalf-pregate-opened) Candidate α); §3 N1 (signatures produce hypotheses, not definitive claims; demotion is structural); §3 N3 (demote-* CLIs operator-elected per [`§0119`](#0119--cli-orphan-cleanup-audit-symmetry-authscope-rfc-open-question-4-discharged-via-operator-opt-in); Layer A + Layer B advisory per [`§0141`](#0141--layer-b-service-tier-implementation-resolution-conservative-defaults-bundle-adopted-a1-internal-package--b1-on-the-fly--c1-substrate-global--d1-transient-demotereport--e1-advisory-like-layer-a--f3-cli-operator-supplied-with-bundled-defaults) E1); §4 criterion 1 (sub-benchmarks mechanically observable via substrate replay; instrumentation by subtype × fonte × morfologia structurally-checkable at the marshalling boundary).

  Falsifiability discipline: comprovation criterion produces non-ambiguous verdict at month 5–6 per the six-outcome falsifiability table in the RFC. Each outcome is informative (substrate property confirmed, F3 insufficient, parameter miscalibration, etc.) — not a checkbox.

  Subordination discipline: RFC subordinate to Charter v0.7.2, Ontology, Architecture, and prior accepted RFCs. RFC explicitly disclaims modifications to canonical-serialization-contract, technology selections, and frozen Charter sections.

- **Consequences:**
  - [`docs/rfcs/draft/domain-pack-v0-1-anti-bot-atlas.md`](../rfcs/draft/domain-pack-v0-1-anti-bot-atlas.md) opens at framing-PR phase. Status `discussion (framing PR; substantive phase pending evidence-file Phase 2–5 deliberation; resolution pending decision-log entry)`.
  - [`docs/rfcs/discussion/domain-pack-v0-1-evidence.md`](../rfcs/discussion/domain-pack-v0-1-evidence.md) opens with Phase 1 (scope + dependency surface + posture statement + implementation surface inventory).
  - Subsequent F-code work proceeds under ordinary RFC discipline. Each F-code's first commit (F1.NetworkObservation in month 1) begins after framing PR merges; sub-decisions per F-code resolve through evidence-file Phase 2–5 deliberation.
  - **Two separate ontology-revision RFCs anticipated for opening**: `ontology-revision-phenomenon-vs-record-reconciliation` (when F1 has two sources stable; ~month 4–5); `ontology-revision-authentication-class-typing` (when F1 has three modalities stable; ~month 2–3). Both proposed for registration in [`entity-model.md` OMQ section](../ontology/entity-model.md#open-modeling-questions).
  - **F6 substrate-read contract** is a new architecture artifact to be drafted in parallel with F3 (month 4–5). Parallel to canonical-serialization-contract; defines read semantics + reproducibility guarantees + export format for audit-grade navigation + statelessness invariant.
  - **Methodological observation 1 — First domain-pack RFC introduces a new RFC category.** Prior RFC categories: `charter-amendment`, `ontology-revision`, `operational-spec`, `architecture`. **Fifth category opens here: `domain-pack`**. The hybrid structure (constitutional framing + executable criterion) follows from the dual nature — opening structural pressure on the substrate + committing to a six-month execution plan. Neither precedent alone covers the scope. Future domain packs (if anti-bot is not the only domain pursued) inherit this hybrid pattern.
  - **Methodological observation 2 — Form-vs-parameter-vs-implementation tripartite extends to four layers.** Per [`§0011`](#0011--q4-resolution-staged-combination-demotion-criterion-layer-a--deferred-layer-b) + [`§0141`](#0141--layer-b-service-tier-implementation-resolution-conservative-defaults-bundle-adopted-a1-internal-package--b1-on-the-fly--c1-substrate-global--d1-transient-demotereport--e1-advisory-like-layer-a--f3-cli-operator-supplied-with-bundled-defaults) Methodological Observation 1, the tripartite was form (Charter + Ontology) + parameters (operational-spec at contract layer) + implementation (operational-spec at service layer). This entry adds the **fourth layer: applied domain** on top of implementation. Pattern catalogue: form (RFCs producing Charter/Ontology amendments) → parameters (RFCs producing canonical-serialization-contract revisions) → implementation (RFCs producing service-tier code) → applied domain (RFCs producing concrete domain packs on top of all three).
  - **Methodological observation 3 — Cross-instance Claude collaboration with tier 1/2/3 verification rule.** The framing was produced via deliberation between this Claude Code instance + an external chat-Claude instance, with explicit verification protocol: tier 1 (letter+number citations) require grep before citation; tier 2 (number-only) require enumeration verification; tier 3 (content-claim on entries) require integral entry-reading. Two enactions validated the rule mid-deliberation. **Future cross-instance collaboration on Charter/Ontology surface work should adopt the same protocol.** The asymmetric blast radius of tier-3 miscites (a single content-claim error can propagate into multiple subsequent artifacts) justifies the verification overhead.
  - **Methodological observation 4 — Anticipated-OMQ declaration before work begins (extension of [`§0137`](#0137--patch-amendment-v071-charter-26--3-0034--0136-staleanchor-correction-0136-anchorfidelity-observation-discharged) Methodological observation 3 to RFC-opening discipline).** The RFC explicitly enumerates five anticipated OMQs (three on existing surfaces + two new requiring registration). This is parallel to the anchor-inventory checklist that [`§0142`](#0142--patch-amendment-v072-charter-23--24--26-q2q3q5-staleanchor-sweep-0137-methodological-observation-3-first-deliberate-enaction) first enacted deliberately — declaring expected pressures before work begins so that surfacing is recognized as expected, not surprise. **Future domain-pack and operational-spec RFCs should include an Anticipated OMQs section.**
  - **Window timeline.** Month 1: F1.NetworkObservation + CIC-IDS adapter + honeypot legal-review begins (critical path). Month 2: F1.BehavioralObservation + synthetic generator v0 + CIC-IDS complete. Month 2–3: F1.AttestationObservation + F1.BrowserObservation (may need sub-RFC for discriminated-union decision) + F4 OMQ opens. Month 4–5: F3 AutomationGroup minimum viable + F6 substrate-read contract drafted + F2 extends + phenomenon-vs-record OMQ surfaces + Sub-benchmark 1 attempt. Month 5–6: F3 BehavioralCluster extends + F6 audit-grade navigability + Sub-benchmark 2 attempt + §0022 final capture.

- **Supersession:** No prior decision-log entry superseded. Cross-Claude posture deliberation (D1/D2/D3/D4) is exogenous input to this entry — recorded here as load-bearing context, not subject to internal entry revision.

## `0144` — F1.NetworkObservation: discriminated-union typing over five sub-modalities (tcp_fingerprint, tls_ja4, http2_frame_pattern, dns_pattern, ip_asn); first proto-definition landing under Domain Pack v0.1

- **Status:** accepted.
- **Date:** 2026-05-23.
- **Context:** [`§0143`](#0143--domain-pack-v01-anti-bot-atlas-framing-pr-opened-first-applied-domain-vertical-on-the-substrate-hybrid-ontologyrevision--operationalspec-rfc-structure) opened Domain Pack v0.1 anti-bot atlas with F1 (typed observation taxonomy) as month-1 P0 immediate. F1 introduces four Cat I observation subtypes — NetworkObservation, BehavioralObservation, AttestationObservation, BrowserObservation — to replace the existing opaque `NetworkEvent` Cat I generic. This entry records the first of those four: F1.NetworkObservation. Pre-condition discharged: RFC Domain Pack v0.1 framing PR merged at [`§0143`](#0143--domain-pack-v01-anti-bot-atlas-framing-pr-opened-first-applied-domain-vertical-on-the-substrate-hybrid-ontologyrevision--operationalspec-rfc-structure).

  Human-cravada constitutional framing for NetworkObservation: **discriminated union (proto3 oneof) over five sub-modalities** — `tcp_fingerprint`, `tls_ja4`, `http2_frame_pattern`, `dns_pattern`, `ip_asn`. Five sub-modality proto messages (`NetworkTcpFingerprint`, `NetworkTlsJa4`, `NetworkHttp2FramePattern`, `NetworkDnsPattern`, `NetworkIpAsn`) carried as oneof variants of the `NetworkObservation` envelope. Envelope carries invariant fields (`observed_at`, `actor_ref`, `endpoint_ref`, `collector_ref`); sub-modality variants carry the modality-specific payload.

- **Decision:** Six proto-definitions land in `schemas/events/v1/` under the existing flat-directory convention (NOT a new sub-directory; aligns with `automation_group_*` × 6 lifecycle files precedent): `network_observation.proto` (envelope) + `network_tcp_fingerprint.proto` + `network_tls_ja4.proto` + `network_http2_frame_pattern.proto` + `network_dns_pattern.proto` + `network_ip_asn.proto`. Each sub-modality proto declares the structurally-minimum field set to support the named anti-bot fingerprinting / pattern-detection layer (TCP layer per p0f-style; TLS handshake per FoxIO JA4 spec; HTTP/2 frame patterns per RFC 7540; DNS query patterns over a window — anonymized; IP/ASN provenance with geo).

  Constitutional discipline applied at proto-definition layer:

  - **`actor_ref` per [`§0023`](#0023--q2-identity-tiers-inceptionphase-singletier-actor_ref-adopted)** — declared on the NetworkObservation envelope as a single-tier string field (optional; empty = unattributed observation). Sub-modality variants inherit attribution via the envelope; no per-variant `actor_ref`.
  - **content-addressable BLAKE3 identifier per [§2.1](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#21-observational-integrity)** — satisfied by the canonical-serialization-contract Marshal+Hash pipeline ([`§0136`](#0136--canonical-serialization-contract-revision-paireddimension----graph--l-bc-or-consolidated-at-the-contract-layer-26-paireddimension-operational-discharge)); NOT a per-record proto field. Tier-3 refinement of the original framing spec recorded for precision: the BLAKE3 identifier is a property of the serialization pipeline, not a field embedded in each proto.
  - **hash-reconstructible independently per F6 substrate-read contract anticipated in [`§0143`](#0143--domain-pack-v01-anti-bot-atlas-framing-pr-opened-first-applied-domain-vertical-on-the-substrate-hybrid-ontologyrevision--operationalspec-rfc-structure)** — operationalized by enforcing zero references to external state in any sub-modality proto. Every field is self-contained scalar / repeated scalar / sub-message; no reference to other substrate records (the IngestionEvent precedent of `primary_event_hash` does NOT replicate here — NetworkObservation is the primary, not a paired record).
  - **Paired-dimension exclusion per [§2.6 BC3](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#26-evidential-independence-integrity)** — NetworkObservation + its 5 sub-modality types declare NEITHER `confidence` NOR `evidential_independence` fields. `validatePairedDimensionCommitment` per [`§0140`](#0140--canonical-serialization-contract-revision-paireddimension-marshallingboundary-enforcement-corrected-allowpartial-false-no-op-for-proto3-acknowledged-explicit-canonical-package-check-installed) selects subject types by structural detection ("declares BOTH confidence + evidential_independence fields"). NetworkObservation is structurally excluded. Tier-3 refinement of the original framing spec recorded for precision: this is structural exclusion (validator does not apply), not "consistent absence enforcement" (which would imply a check that the fields are absent — they are simply not declared).
  - **Canonical-serialization-contract enforcement per [`§0140`](#0140--canonical-serialization-contract-revision-paireddimension-marshallingboundary-enforcement-corrected-allowpartial-false-no-op-for-proto3-acknowledged-explicit-canonical-package-check-installed)** — Marshal+Hash via `canonical.Marshal` + `canonical.Hash` pipeline. Test coverage: round-trip determinism per sub-modality, oneof exhaustiveness (5 distinct hashes for envelope-equivalent observations), actor_ref discipline, collector_ref discipline.

  `collector_ref` envelope field (field number 4) is introduced **pre-emptively** as the structural seed for the phenomenon-vs-record reconciliation OMQ anticipated in [`§0143`](#0143--domain-pack-v01-anti-bot-atlas-framing-pr-opened-first-applied-domain-vertical-on-the-substrate-hybrid-ontologyrevision--operationalspec-rfc-structure). The OMQ opens formally for committee resolution when F1 has two ingestion sources stable (per §0143 trigger); the field exists at landing so that subsequent records produced by different ingestion sources are immediately distinguishable at the substrate layer. Compatible with Methodological observation 2 below (anticipate ≠ pre-resolve): the structural slot is present; the OMQ resolution remains future work.

- **Constitutional review:** No Charter prose modified. No Charter invariant amended. No new Charter invariant. The RFC consumes Charter v0.7.2 frozen state as given. Each invariant consumed but not modified: §2.1 (substrate immutability inherited; F1.NetworkObservation produces Cat I substrate records), §2.2 (Cat I primary observation per entity-model.md §Category I), §2.3 (provenance chain terminates at Cat I primaries — NetworkObservation IS such a primary), §2.6 BC3 (paired-dimension subject set excludes observation records — confirmed by structural detection in `validatePairedDimensionCommitment`).

  Falsifiability discipline: each constitutional claim above is structurally observable. The structural-exclusion claim for paired-dimension is mechanized by `TestPairedDimensionSubjectSet_StructuralDetection` (existing test in `coverage_test.go`) which automatically picks up the new `network-observation` messageFactory registration and verifies the type is NOT detected as paired-dimension-subject. Round-trip determinism is mechanized by `TestNetworkObservation_RoundTripPerModality`. Oneof discriminator hash separation is mechanized by `TestNetworkObservation_OneofExhaustiveness`. Hash-stability of `actor_ref` discipline is mechanized by `TestNetworkObservation_ActorRefDiscipline`. Hash-stability of `collector_ref` discipline is mechanized by `TestNetworkObservation_CollectorRefDiscipline`.

- **Consequences:**
  - Six proto-definitions land in `schemas/events/v1/`: `network_observation.proto`, `network_tcp_fingerprint.proto`, `network_tls_ja4.proto`, `network_http2_frame_pattern.proto`, `network_dns_pattern.proto`, `network_ip_asn.proto`.
  - Six generated Go pb.go files in `services/ingestion/internal/genproto/events/v1/`.
  - `messageFactory` in `services/ingestion/internal/canonical/corpus_test.go` extends with `network-observation` entry.
  - New focused test file `services/ingestion/internal/canonical/network_observation_test.go` covering round-trip per modality, oneof exhaustiveness, actor_ref discipline, collector_ref discipline.
  - Golden corpus extends with six fixtures: `network-observation-{minimal,tcp-fingerprint,tls-ja4,http2-frame-pattern,dns-pattern,ip-asn}.{json,bin,hash}`.
  - `services/ingestion/Makefile` `generate` target adds the six new proto files to the explicit enumeration.
  - **Schemas-evolution event per the canonical-serialization-contract §Schemas-Evolution Events boundary** — six new proto message types added; corpus regenerated; goldens committed. No existing proto modified; no breaking change to existing corpus.
  - Legacy `NetworkEvent` proto (`network_event.proto`) **NOT removed** in this entry. NetworkEvent and NetworkObservation coexist: NetworkEvent is the legacy opaque shape (carried for backward compatibility with any external collectors that produce the legacy form); NetworkObservation is the typed form for F3 signature consumption. Future entry may deprecate NetworkEvent once all collectors migrate; not in scope here.
  - **Methodological observation 1 — Discriminated-union over opaque envelope is the structural framing for F1 modalities.** Constitutional framing decision (a) cravada by human: strong typing pressures F3 signature engines to name explicitly which sub-modalities each signature consumes; opaque envelope would replicate the existing `NetworkEvent` pattern without pressuring substrate in new direction. The choice is part of the epistemic yield of the "comprovar" posture cravada in Domain Pack v0.1 — F3 signatures cannot quietly consume fields that are not structurally named at substrate.
  - **Methodological observation 2 — Anticipated OMQs in [`§0143`](#0143--domain-pack-v01-anti-bot-atlas-framing-pr-opened-first-applied-domain-vertical-on-the-substrate-hybrid-ontologyrevision--operationalspec-rfc-structure) open in discussion phase ONLY under empirical surface-pressure per [`§0022`](#0022--implementation-pivot-64-amendment--0003-reversal-authorization--2426-posture-shift); speculative framing without empirical pressure violates empirical-grounding criterion.** Concrete example with authentication-class-typing OMQ: §0143 explicitly named "when F1 has three modalities stable" as the trigger for the OMQ to open. F1.NetworkObservation lands **without** opening the authentication-class OMQ; the OMQ opens when BehavioralObservation + AttestationObservation also land and the structural distinction between server-authenticated, client-attested, client-witnessed becomes empirically forced. **Anticipating an OMQ ≠ pre-resolving it; the structural slot for resolution may be reserved (see Consequence on `collector_ref` field) but the resolution itself awaits pressure.**
  - **Methodological observation 3 — Discriminated-union choice in F1.NetworkObservation establishes pattern for BehavioralObservation, AttestationObservation, BrowserObservation.** Structural coherence will demand `oneof` discriminator similar in the three other Cat I modalities. AttestationObservation **likely requires sub-RFC própria**: the five protocols enumerated in [`§0143`](#0143--domain-pack-v01-anti-bot-atlas-framing-pr-opened-first-applied-domain-vertical-on-the-substrate-hybrid-ontologyrevision--operationalspec-rfc-structure) (Apple Private Access Tokens, Google Privacy Pass, Cloudflare Turnstile, WebAuthn, FIDO2) each have distinct format, lifecycle, verification path; unifying into a single Cat I type via discriminated union may produce 5 sub-modality protos OR may force a discriminated-union-of-discriminated-unions structure. Anotado as anticipated pressure for AttestationObservation landing (per §0143 timeline: month 2–3).
  - **Methodological observation 4 — OMQ candidate: cross-sub-modal correlation in provenance chain.** When F3 produces signatures that consume multiple sub-modalities of NetworkObservation (e.g., AutomationGroup correlating `tcp_fingerprint` + `tls_ja4` + `ip_asn` for a single actor), the `influenced_by` semantics per [§2.4](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#24-inferential-influence-disclosure) may need to represent the cross-sub-modal correlation explicitly. The current `influenced_by` chain is per-hypothesis (not per-feature-subset); a hypothesis formed from cross-sub-modal correlation has its `influenced_by` reference the hypothesis as a whole, losing the granular dependency on each modality. Anotado for surface during F3 month 4–5. May resolve via existing chain semantics (acceptable lossy granularity) or may require new structural surface (likely a new ontology-revision RFC if the latter).
  - **Methodological observation 5 — `collector_ref` envelope field is pre-emptive structural slot for phenomenon-vs-record reconciliation OMQ.** §0143 anticipated the OMQ; the structural slot lands here pre-emptively (Methodological observation 2 above explicitly allows this distinction). When second ingestion source (synthetic generator OR honeypot) produces NetworkObservation records, the same phenomenon (e.g., the same JA4 fingerprint) may appear as distinct substrate records with different `collector_ref` values. The OMQ asks: should F3 compute over the union (broader coverage, double-counting risk) or filter to unique phenomena (requires reconciliation)? The OMQ formal opening waits for the empirical pressure; the structural slot is present so that resolution does not require schemas-evolution event.

- **Supersession:** No prior decision-log entry superseded. NetworkEvent legacy proto remains in substrate (coexistence).

## `0145` — CIC-IDS-2017 adapter lands: first public adversarial ingestion source integrated; ~18% aggregate coverage empirically confirmed; `flow_record_summary` OMQ candidate surfaced

- **Status:** accepted.
- **Date:** 2026-05-23.
- **Context:** Per [`§0143`](#0143--domain-pack-v01-anti-bot-atlas-framing-pr-opened-first-applied-domain-vertical-on-the-substrate-hybrid-ontologyrevision--operationalspec-rfc-structure) D2 (three-source-parallel ingestion strategy: public + synthetic + honeypot) and [`§0144`](#0144--f1networkobservation-discriminatedunion-typing-over-five-submodalities-tcp_fingerprint-tls_ja4-http2_frame_pattern-dns_pattern-ip_asn-first-protodefinition-landing-under-domain-pack-v01) F1.NetworkObservation discriminated-union typing, this entry records the landing of the **first public adversarial source** — CIC-IDS-2017 (Sharafaldin et al., ICISSP 2018) — as a typed adapter under `services/ingestion/internal/adapters/cic_ids/`. Pre-condition discharged: F1.NetworkObservation proto-definitions merged in main per [`§0144`](#0144--f1networkobservation-discriminatedunion-typing-over-five-submodalities-tcp_fingerprint-tls_ja4-http2_frame_pattern-dns_pattern-ip_asn-first-protodefinition-landing-under-domain-pack-v01) (PR #164).

  Per [`§0144`](#0144--f1networkobservation-discriminatedunion-typing-over-five-submodalities-tcp_fingerprint-tls_ja4-http2_frame_pattern-dns_pattern-ip_asn-first-protodefinition-landing-under-domain-pack-v01) CIC-IDS coverage preview, ~18% aggregate coverage was predicted across the five NetworkObservation sub-modalities. This adapter empirically confirms the prediction.

- **Decision:** Adapter implementation lands as `services/ingestion/internal/adapters/cic_ids/` Go package with three surfaces: `ParseRow` (CSV-row → typed `FlowRecord`), `ToObservations` (`FlowRecord` → `[]*NetworkObservation`), `Ingest` (streaming end-to-end with substrate commit via `ingest.Ingester`). Mapping documented exhaustively at [`docs/adapters/cic-ids-mapping.md`](../adapters/cic-ids-mapping.md) per [`§0143`](#0143--domain-pack-v01-anti-bot-atlas-framing-pr-opened-first-applied-domain-vertical-on-the-substrate-hybrid-ontologyrevision--operationalspec-rfc-structure) adapter discipline.

  Coverage realized:

  | Sub-modality | Estimate ([`§0143`](#0143--domain-pack-v01-anti-bot-atlas-framing-pr-opened-first-applied-domain-vertical-on-the-substrate-hybrid-ontologyrevision--operationalspec-rfc-structure)) | Realized | Notes |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `ip_asn` | ~50% | **clean** | Two observations per flow (src + dst sides); ASN/geo deferred to enrichment (`lookup_source = ""`) |
  | `tcp_fingerprint` | ~30% | **partial with documented semantic loss** | TCP-flag-counts → TCP-flag-byte-sequence approximation; TCP options absent (CICFlowMeter does not preserve); `Init_Win_bytes_forward` → window_size when present |
  | `tls_ja4` | 0% | 0% | Dataset does not expose TLS ClientHello fingerprints |
  | `http2_frame_pattern` | 0% | 0% | HTTP-layer frame patterns not in flow-level features |
  | `dns_pattern` | ~10% | 0% in this version | Protocol = 17 + DstPort = 53 identifies DNS flows but QTYPE/RCODE not preserved; future revision may add anonymized derivation |

  Aggregate realized coverage matches the §0143 prediction (~18%). The bulk of CICFlowMeter features (FLOW-STATISTICS class: durations, packet length stats, IAT stats, byte rates, ratios) does NOT map to any current NetworkObservation sub-modality. **This is the empirical surface for the `flow_record_summary` OMQ candidate** per Consequences below.

  Constitutional discipline applied:

  - **`collector_ref` operationally exercised.** Every observation emitted carries `collector_ref = "cic-ids-2017-adapter:v1"`. This operationally exercises the structural slot introduced pre-emptively at [`§0144`](#0144--f1networkobservation-discriminatedunion-typing-over-five-submodalities-tcp_fingerprint-tls_ja4-http2_frame_pattern-dns_pattern-ip_asn-first-protodefinition-landing-under-domain-pack-v01) (e). When second source (synthetic or honeypot) emits observations with distinct `collector_ref` values, the phenomenon-vs-record reconciliation OMQ formally opens for committee resolution per [`§0143`](#0143--domain-pack-v01-anti-bot-atlas-framing-pr-opened-first-applied-domain-vertical-on-the-substrate-hybrid-ontologyrevision--operationalspec-rfc-structure) trigger.
  - **Label column NOT consumed.** CIC-IDS `Label` column carries attack-class annotation (`BENIGN`, `DoS-Slowloris`, etc.). The adapter explicitly does NOT commit Labels to substrate per [§3 N1](../charter/constitutional-charter.md#3-non-goals) (no truth at substrate). Labels are operator ground-truth annotations for downstream F3 signature evaluation, preserved out-of-band.
  - **Substrate-Writer Serialization inherited.** Adapter consumes `ingest.Ingester.Append`; inherits the per-process write serialization per [`docs/architecture/concurrency-pattern.md`](../architecture/concurrency-pattern.md) §Substrate-Writer Serialization. No new concurrency surface introduced.
  - **Idempotent re-ingest.** Substrate commit is content-addressed; re-ingesting the same CSV produces identical hashes and substrate `PRIMARY KEY` conflict makes re-commit a no-op. Operationally tested at `TestIngest_EndToEnd_SampleCSV` (synthetic fixture).

- **Constitutional review:** No Charter prose modified. No Charter invariant amended. No new Charter invariant. Each invariant consumed but not modified: §2.1 (Cat I substrate immutability for emitted NetworkObservation records); §2.3 (provenance chain terminates at Cat I primaries — NetworkObservation IS such a primary); §3 N1 (Label column excluded from substrate — no truth at substrate); §3 N3 (adapter does not perform autonomous irreversible action — operator invokes ingestion explicitly).

  Falsifiability discipline: each adapter behavior is structurally observable via the test suite. `TestIngest_EndToEnd_SampleCSV` asserts exact counts of parsed/rejected/committed/per-sub-modality observations against the synthetic CSV fixture; `TestToObservations_TCPFlow_Emits3` asserts the per-flow observation cardinality for TCP flows; `TestToObservations_UDPFlow_Emits2` asserts UDP flows emit only `ip_asn` pair (no `tcp_fingerprint`); `TestTcpFlagSequenceFromCounts_CanonicalOrder` asserts the canonical TCP-byte order (SYN → FIN → RST → PSH → ACK → URG → ECE → CWE).

- **Consequences:**
  - `services/ingestion/internal/adapters/cic_ids/` Go package lands with `cic_ids.go`, `columns.go`, `cic_ids_test.go`, `testdata/sample.csv`.
  - [`docs/adapters/cic-ids-mapping.md`](../adapters/cic-ids-mapping.md) lands with exhaustive column-by-column mapping table + semantic-loss documentation + OMQ-candidate surface.
  - **No new proto types.** Adapter consumes existing F1.NetworkObservation per [`§0144`](#0144--f1networkobservation-discriminatedunion-typing-over-five-submodalities-tcp_fingerprint-tls_ja4-http2_frame_pattern-dns_pattern-ip_asn-first-protodefinition-landing-under-domain-pack-v01).
  - **No schemas-evolution event.** No proto-definition modified; no corpus regeneration needed.
  - **CLI wiring deferred.** This PR provides the library surface only. CLI command (e.g. `cmd/ingest-cic-ids/`) is a follow-on PR. Rationale: keeping the adapter PR scoped to library + tests + mapping; CLI wiring depends on operator workflow decisions that are best deliberated as separate ticket.
  - **NEW OMQ candidate empirically surfaced: `flow_record_summary` modality.** The FLOW-STATISTICS class of CICFlowMeter features (~60+ columns: durations, packet length statistics, IAT statistics, byte/packet rates, segment sizes, active/idle stats, down/up ratios) does NOT map to any current NetworkObservation sub-modality. **Propose opening separate `ontology-revision-flow-record-summary-modality` RFC** when the second ingestion source confirms the gap is structural (not specific to CICFlowMeter). Compatible with [`§0144`](#0144--f1networkobservation-discriminatedunion-typing-over-five-submodalities-tcp_fingerprint-tls_ja4-http2_frame_pattern-dns_pattern-ip_asn-first-protodefinition-landing-under-domain-pack-v01) Methodological observation 2 (anticipate ≠ pre-resolve): the OMQ is empirically pressured, not pre-empted.
  - **§0144 (e) `collector_ref` slot operationally exercised.** The phenomenon-vs-record reconciliation OMQ now has its first ingestion source producing records under a non-empty `collector_ref`. When the second source produces records under a distinct `collector_ref`, the OMQ formally opens per §0143 trigger.
  - **Methodological observation 1 — §0143 + §0144 coverage estimate predicted reality.** The ~18% aggregate coverage estimate at framing-PR time matched the empirical realization at adapter-landing time, with sub-modality breakdown also matching (ip_asn clean; tcp_fingerprint partial; tls_ja4 + http2_frame_pattern zero; dns_pattern lower than estimated). **Pattern validated: dataset-level coverage estimation in framing PR can be predictive when the dataset's feature taxonomy is well-documented.** Future framing PRs for adapter work should include coverage estimates against the relevant proto-definitions; the predictive accuracy here justifies the framing-PR cost.
  - **Methodological observation 2 — Semantic-loss documentation is part of adapter discipline.** Per the mapping doc: every CIC-IDS column that maps with semantic loss (e.g., TCP-flag-counts → TCP-flag-sequence approximation; per-direction window size collapsed to single window) is explicitly named at the column-mapping table, not buried in code comments. **Future adapters should follow the same per-column semantic-loss discipline; loss-detection becomes a falsifiability axis (auditor verifies the documented loss matches code behavior).**
  - **Methodological observation 3 — Empirical OMQ surfaces via counter discipline, not retrospective analysis.** `Report.FlowStatisticsDropped` counter increments per row, surfacing the volume of unmapped features at ingest time. Operators see the gap empirically as a number; the structural OMQ (`flow_record_summary`) is the named pressure. **Future adapters should expose per-class "dropped feature" counters when the dataset's feature set exceeds the consumed sub-modality coverage. The counter is the empirical pressure surface; the OMQ is the structural articulation.**
  - **Methodological observation 4 — Adapter pattern established for synthetic + honeypot sources.** This adapter's three-function surface (`ParseRow` + `ToObservations` + `Ingest`) is the template for future adapters. Synthetic generator (mês 2 per §0143 timeline) and honeypot collector (mês 4-5 yield window) will follow the same pattern with different parsers but identical `ToObservations` + `Ingest` shape. **Future adapter PRs should reference this entry as the pattern precedent and document only divergences.**

- **Supersession:** No prior decision-log entry superseded. First instance of a public-adversarial-source ingestion adapter; first operational exercise of `collector_ref` slot from [`§0144`](#0144--f1networkobservation-discriminatedunion-typing-over-five-submodalities-tcp_fingerprint-tls_ja4-http2_frame_pattern-dns_pattern-ip_asn-first-protodefinition-landing-under-domain-pack-v01) (e).
